Each component has its own network stack, so a variable that works for one does nothing for another. Only the Linux distributor row was tested, with BusyBox 1.37.0 of alpine:3 against a stub proxy, not a real corporate proxy. The other rows follow from how each program is written, and the CI does not test them.

Component Proxy variables Your own certificate authority
The Docker engine of each node (every image pull) The engine’s own settings: HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY in a systemd drop-in of docker.service, or proxies in daemon.json. The stack files set nothing The node’s trust store. For a private registry, /etc/docker/certs.d/<registry>/ca.crt
runner-distributor on Linux Its wget is BusyBox: it reads only lowercase http_proxy, sends an https:// URL as GET https://... (not CONNECT), and ignores no_proxy. HTTPS_PROXY does nothing. Use a mirror that the node reaches without a proxy The Alpine image’s CA bundle only. Use an http:// mirror with the SHA-256 list, or an image of your own
runner-distributor-windows HTTPS_PROXY only, for every download. NO_PROXY is not read The container’s Windows certificate store, which lacks your authority. Use an http:// mirror with the SHA-256 list, or an image of your own
token-proxy A Go program: HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, NO_PROXY apply to its calls to CircleCI, set under the service’s environment. Swarm DNS lookups ignore them Linux: SSL_CERT_FILE replaces the image’s public roots, so mount one bundle with the public roots and yours (a Swarm config) and point SSL_CERT_FILE at it. Windows: the container’s Windows certificate store
The runner and task agent Go programs: the same variables under the class’s environment, inherited by jobs. Add token-proxy (Windows: token-proxy-windows) to NO_PROXY so calls to the proxy stay on the overlay network The class image: add the authority to its system store (Images). SSL_CERT_FILE replaces a Go program’s roots on Unix. On Windows, Go reads the Windows store, so the authority must be in the image
The steps of a job Whatever the job’s tools read. Class variables are inherited The image’s system store

What to copy into the site

For a site that reaches CircleCI through a proxy, or mirrors what it can, copy in the release bundle and SHA256SUMS, the images by digest (the proxy image with its signature via cosign copy), the runner tarballs per node architecture (the pinned version and the one before it, plus manifest.json for a floating version), on Windows the two Git downloads, and for a MicroVM class the Kata tarball.

Verify a release without internet

cosign verify-blob and cosign verify fetch the Sigstore trust root over the network by default, and this project has not tested an offline verification. Verify on a host with access (Verify a release), copy the verified files and the images by digest in, and check them on the site with sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS and the digests the verified release names. Recent cosign versions can also verify against a trusted root that you carry in (--trusted-root): test it with a known release first.

Uninstall

  1. Remove the stack. Swarm sends SIGTERM to the tasks, so running jobs get the grace period to finish:

    docker stack rm runners

  2. Remove the secrets (<service>-token of every class you deployed) and the persistent-class volumes:

    docker secret rm linux-default-token runner-placeholder-token
docker volume rm runners_persistent-home runners_proxy-state

    The Windows persistent class volume is runners_windows-persistent-cache, and the Windows proxy keeps its state in runners_proxy-state too.

    The volume runners_runner-bin holds the runner (and Git on Windows) and stays on every node after docker stack rm. Remove it on every node, on Windows after the last container of the stack is gone:

    docker volume rm runners_runner-bin

  3. Remove the nodes from the Swarm: docker swarm leave on each worker, then docker swarm leave --force on the last manager. No node has files outside Docker to remove.

item.title: Quickstart on Linux
item.description:
Go from nothing to a first job on one Linux node in five steps. The page sets up one class, linux-default, and installs nothing on the node by hand: a service of the stack installs the runner.

Note

This is a CircleCI Labs project, not supported by CircleCI support. It is a 0.x release: read the release notes before you upgrade. What is tested says how it is checked. One token proxy runs on a manager, so while it is down no new job starts: use three managers in production.

Before you start

  • A node with Ubuntu LTS, Docker Engine 24 or later, curl, a clock on NTP, and outbound HTTPS (what needs internet). Prepare each node shows how to install Docker.
  • The CircleCI CLI 1.4.0 or later, on your workstation or on the node.
  • An organization admin who accepted the CircleCI Runner Terms.
  • A runner namespace. If your organization has none, create one with circleci namespace create <NAMESPACE> --org <ORG>.

Replace <NAMESPACE> with your runner namespace, and <ORG> with your organization slug such as gh/my-org, or its UUID. Run the commands on the node as a user in the docker group, or add sudo.

Steps

  1. Create a resource class and a token. The command prints the token once: keep it for step 3.

    circleci auth login
circleci runner resource-class create <NAMESPACE>/linux-default --org <ORG> --generate-token

  2. On the node, download the latest release, and start a one-node Swarm that listens on the loopback address. To verify the release signature first, see Install on Linux > Verify a release.

    version=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/releases/latest)
version=${version##*/v}
curl -fsSL "https://github.com/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/releases/download/v${version}/machine-runner-swarm-${version}.tar.gz" | tar -xz
cd "machine-runner-swarm-${version}"
    sudo linux/setup.sh --check --swarm-init

    No other node can join this Swarm, and the runners share the node with the token proxy, so use it for a trial. For a cluster, follow Multi-Node Clusters instead.

  3. Create the secrets. The first command asks for the token from step 1 (hidden input). The token goes to the token proxy only. The second creates the placeholder that the runners read instead of a token.

    sudo linux/setup.sh --secret linux-default
printf %s machine-runner-swarm-placeholder | sudo linux/setup.sh --secret runner-placeholder

  4. Deploy the stack, and check it. docker stack deploy does not wait, so the replicas need a minute to start.

    sudo linux/setup.sh --deploy
    sudo docker stack services runners
circleci runner instance list --org <ORG> --resource-class <NAMESPACE>/linux-default

    The stack is up when runners_linux-default shows 2/2, runners_token-proxy shows 1/1, and the CLI lists an instance with the status online. If a replica stays Pending, the node is too small: it needs 4 CPUs and 8 GB, so set a lower deploy.replicas (Size the limits, A task stays pending).

  5. Run a job. Save this as .circleci/config.yml in a project of your organization, replace my-namespace with your namespace, then commit and push. The same file is examples/linux-hello.yml.

    version: 2.1

jobs:
 hello:
 machine: true
 resource_class: my-namespace/linux-default
 steps:
 - run:
 name: Show where this job runs
 command: |
 echo "runner: $CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME"
 if [ -e /tmp/hello-marker ]; then echo "the container was reused"; exit 1; fi
 touch /tmp/hello-marker
 echo "clean container: no marker from an earlier job"

workflows:
 hello:
 jobs:
 - hello

    Run the workflow twice. Both runs pass, because Swarm starts a new container for each job.

Next

  • Install on Linux: every step by hand, RHEL, release verification, and upgrades. Before production, copy linux/stack to a directory of your own and deploy that copy (Review the stack file).
  • Concepts: services as resource classes, the token proxy, and the job lifecycle.
  • Resource Classes: add classes, and change sizes and replicas.
  • Security: choose the default or the hardened class before you give a class to a team.
  • Operations: pin or roll back the runner, rotate tokens, and run the cluster.
  • Troubleshooting: symptoms, causes, and fixes.

item.title: Resource classes
item.description:
Each Swarm service in a stack file is one CircleCI resource class, named <namespace>/<service>, and deploy.replicas is how many jobs it runs at once. This page lists the shipped sizes, then how to add a class, choose replicas, run a persistent class, enable Rerun job with SSH, and read the stack variables.

Size the limits

Limits cap what a runner can use. Reservations tell the scheduler how much room a replica needs, and the stack sets them equal. A reservation is held whether or not the replica runs a job, so you pay for the peak. A service with no reservation still has the limit shown.

Service File Replicas Reserved for each replica Limit, when it differs
linux-default runners.yaml 2 2 CPUs, 4 GB
token-proxy runners.yaml 1 0.1 CPU, 32 MB 0.5 CPU, 128 MB
runner-distributor runners.yaml One for each Linux node Nothing 0.5 CPU, 256 MB
linux-java classes-extra.yaml 1 4 CPUs, 8 GB
linux-hardened classes-extra.yaml 1 2 CPUs, 4 GB
linux-docker-build docker-build.yaml 1 4 CPUs, 8 GB
linux-microvm microvm.yaml 2 2 CPUs, 4 GB The VM adds overhead of its own, not measured here
linux-microvm-docker microvm.yaml 1 4 CPUs, 8 GB The same
microvm-dns microvm.yaml 2 Nothing 0.5 CPU, 128 MB
microvm-netkeep microvm.yaml One for each microVM node Nothing 0.2 CPU, 256 MB
linux-persistent persistent.yaml 1 4 CPUs, 8 GB
linux-default-ssh ssh-rerun.yaml 1 2 CPUs, 4 GB
windows-default runners.yaml (Windows) 2 2 CPUs, 4 GB
token-proxy-windows runners.yaml (Windows) 1 Nothing 1 CPU, 512 MB
runner-distributor-windows runners.yaml (Windows) One for each Windows node Nothing 1 CPU, 1 GB
windows-custom, windows-docker-build, windows-default-ssh Add-on files (Windows) 1 each 2 CPUs, 4 GB
windows-persistent persistent.yaml (Windows) 1 4 CPUs, 8 GB

The shipped runners.yaml reserves 4.1 CPUs and a little over 8 GB on Linux, and 4 CPUs and 8 GB on Windows, before the operating system, Docker and the distributor. classes-extra.yaml adds 6 CPUs and 12 GB.

Setting Linux Windows
limits.cpus Caps CPU Caps CPU. A value above the CPU count of the host is rejected
limits.memory Caps memory. The kernel kills a job that exceeds it Caps memory
limits.pids Caps processes. The files set 4096 Rejected by the Windows engine, so absent
reservations Scheduler only. Extra replicas stay pending instead of overcommitting Scheduler only. The engine never receives it
ulimits nofile 65536, core 0 Rejected by the Windows engine, so absent

Size one runner for the largest job of the class. A job cannot pick a size, so create a second class (for example linux-large) for bigger jobs. The reservations of all replicas on a node must fit in it, with room for the operating system and Docker (for example one CPU and 2 GB). Replicas that do not fit stay Pending.

Swarm cannot limit disk. Jobs share the Docker data disk of the node, so size it for the replicas plus the stopped containers that Swarm keeps (Start Swarm). A Windows node also holds the servercore base image (about 2.2 GB compressed).

Cost. This project has no price of its own. You pay for the nodes at the peak, your CircleCI plan, and the network and storage that jobs use. Runner compute does not use credits, but at least one credit is needed, and self-hosted runner concurrency is a separate limit of your plan (Run jobs on self-hosted runners).

Define a class

The shipped linux/stack/runners.yaml has one class, linux-default. Add other classes to your copy of the stack files (deploy/runners.yaml, as Install on Linux describes) and deploy your copy. linux/stack/classes-extra.yaml is a worked example: it adds linux-java and linux-hardened.

  1. Create the resource class and a token in CircleCI. The class name must equal the service name.

    circleci runner resource-class create <NAMESPACE>/linux-python --org <ORG> --generate-token

  2. Copy the service linux-default in your stack file under another name, and change the name, hostname, CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME and networks as in the example below.

  3. Create the secret <service>-token with the token. Refer to Create the secrets or Create the secrets on Windows.

  4. On Linux, add the class network and secret to the existing token-proxy service. The proxy serves a class for every secret <service>-token that it holds, and finds its runners as tasks.<service>.

  5. Deploy again with the same -c files as before. Swarm creates the new service and leaves the others alone.

    docker stack deploy -c deploy/runners.yaml runners

The runner name must be unique across the runners of your organization. It has at most 64 characters and contains only letters, numbers, ., (, ), _, -, and spaces. A long hostname plus class name can exceed that, and the runner then exits with code 80.

A Linux example, in your copy of runners.yaml, where the anchors *runner, *env, *restart, *update and *placement resolve. First, the service next to linux-default:

services:
 linux-python:
 <<: *runner
 image: cimg/python:3.14
 hostname: "{{.Node.Hostname}}-linux-python-{{.Task.Slot}}"
 environment:
 <<: *env
 CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME: "{{.Node.Hostname}}-linux-python-{{.Task.Slot}}"
 MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO: "true"
 networks: [linux-python]
 cap_drop: [NET_RAW, MKNOD]  # keep NET_RAW dropped: the proxy tells runners apart by source address
 deploy:
 replicas: 2
 restart_policy: *restart
 update_config: *update
 resources:
 limits: {cpus: "2", memory: 4G, pids: 4096}
 reservations: {cpus: "2", memory: 4G}
 placement: *placement

Second, add these lines to the token-proxy: key, which appears once in the file. Do not repeat the key:

 token-proxy:
 secrets:
 # ... the secrets of the classes that are there
 - {source: linux-python-token, target: linux-python-token, uid: "65534", gid: "65534", mode: 0400}
 networks: [linux-default, linux-python]  # every class network, the new one included

Third, declare the network (linux-python: {driver: overlay, driver_opts: {encrypted: "true"}}) under the top-level networks: and the secret (linux-python-token: {external: true}) under secrets:.

A deploy that adds a class secret replaces the proxy task. What the runners see meanwhile is in Restart the proxy. A class that the proxy does not serve gets 403 on every claim, and the proxy log says not a runner of any class. For a hardened class, set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO: "false" with the capability settings of linux-hardened (Concepts).

A class in its own stack file. Write token-proxy there with only the secret and network: Swarm merges files by name. Anchors do not reach into another file, so repeat what *runner sets (user: "0", the entrypoint and its config, the placeholder secret runner-placeholder-token, CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_URL: http://token-proxy:8080, and the read-only volume runner-bin), or copy classes-extra.yaml. The config name carries the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the file, because a Swarm config cannot change (Upgrade to a new release of this repository).

A class on Windows. Copy a service such as windows-default in your copy of windows\stack\runners.yaml, with its two mounts of the volume runner-bin (subpath: current and subpath: 'git\current'). Its CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME is "{{.Node.Hostname}}-windows-<class>-{{.Task.Slot}}", and the file sets no hostname. The secret has no uid, gid, or mode, and the file defines no networks. A single-task class also adds its secret (target <service>-token) to token-proxy-windows, and reads runner-placeholder-token.

Choose replica counts

deploy.replicas is the number of jobs the class runs at the same time.

  1. Estimate the peak number of parallel jobs for the class.
  2. Check that nodes with enough room exist. A replica needs its full reservation on one node.
  3. Add one replica for many very short jobs. A replica needs about 10 seconds between jobs.
  4. Set deploy.replicas in the stack file and deploy again. The file stays the source of truth.

For a quick change, scale the service. The next docker stack deploy resets the count to the file.

docker service scale runners_linux-default=4

Swarm has no autoscaling and this stack adds none. Set replicas: 0 to switch a class off without deleting it, and know that jobs for a class with no runner wait without limit and hold concurrency (Capacity and concurrency). For elastic capacity, use the machine runner orchestrator or CircleCI cloud executors (FAQ).

Persistent mode

Status: experimental. CI runs the persistent class with a fake or idle runner only, and no real job runs on it in CI.

A persistent class runs the runner in continuous mode. One long-lived container claims job after job, and a named volume keeps data between jobs. Use it only for trusted projects that gain a lot from warm caches.

Warning

Continuous mode removes the guarantee of a clean environment. A job can leave files, processes, or settings that later jobs see, and can change what later jobs run. CircleCI rates untrusted jobs on a runner that keeps its environment as the highest risk.

To limit the risk:

  • Use a separate class restricted to named projects with a config policy (CircleCI-side controls), and keep production contexts away from it.
  • Put cleanup steps at the start of its jobs. The runner does not clean the working directory on Linux.
  • Recycle the runner on a schedule.
  • On Linux this class is weaker than the single-task classes: it does not use the token proxy, so the runner holds the real token (The persistent class).

Linux

linux/stack/persistent.yaml defines linux-persistent. It sets CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE: continuous with no idle timeout, mounts the named volume persistent-home at /home/circleci (Swarm copies the image content of that directory into the new volume on first use), and sets CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR to "false", so each job must clean up what an earlier job left (Working directory cleanup).

A volume lives on one node, so the service has the constraint node.hostname == CHANGE-ME. Edit it in your copy (deploy/persistent.yaml) before you deploy.

The runner keeps its class token in its own container, because a continuous runner claims after every job and the proxy allows one claim for each container. The shipped file sets MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO: "false", so jobs have no sudo and cannot read the token file, and the tools that a job needs must be in the image (Images). Set it to "true" in your copy if jobs need sudo, and accept that a job that uses it reads the token and can run a runner of its own on the class.

printf 'api:\n auth_token: %s\n' "$TOKEN" | docker secret create linux-persistent-token -
docker stack deploy -c deploy/runners.yaml -c deploy/persistent.yaml runners

Recycle the runner with a forced update. It drains first (it finishes the running job and takes no new one), and the volume survives. A forced update is also how the class moves to a new runner version.

docker service update --force runners_linux-persistent

Windows

windows\stack\persistent.yaml defines windows-persistent. It sets CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE: continuous with no idle timeout, and mounts the named volume windows-persistent-cache at C:\cache. Point NuGet, npm, and similar caches there with an environment variable in the job. The runner and the jobs use the same account, so the runner cleans the working directory and CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR stays "true".

The service is pinned to nodes with the label machine-runner-swarm.class.windows-persistent=true. Create the secret windows-persistent-token, label the node, and deploy your copy with your copy of the main file:

docker node update --label-add machine-runner-swarm.class.windows-persistent=true <NODE_NAME>
docker stack deploy -c deploy\runners.yaml -c deploy\persistent.yaml runners

Rerun job with SSH

Status: experimental. CI checks that the files parse, merge and keep their contract (the host-mode port 54782, max_replicas_per_node: 1, the advertise address). The Swarm side was proven by hand on Linux with a real runner. No CI test logs in over SSH, and the Windows file is untested.

The add-on files linux/stack/ssh-rerun.yaml and windows\stack\ssh-rerun.yaml define linux-default-ssh and windows-default-ssh. Their runners support Rerun job with SSH, which opens a shell in a running job. The default classes publish no port and cannot serve it.

  • Advertised address. Setting CIRCLECI_RUNNER_SSH_ADVERTISE_ADDR turns the feature on. The task agent then starts an SSH server on the fixed port 54782, and the Enable SSH and Wait for SSH steps show the address. CircleCI only displays it, so it can be any name or IP address your users reach. The add-on files set {{.Node.Hostname}}:54782. If DNS does not resolve node hostnames, use one that does, for example {{.Node.Hostname}}.example.com:54782.
  • Host-mode port. The file publishes 54782 in host mode, so it opens on the node that runs the task (ingress mode would send a connection to any replica, which can be another user’s job). A node has one port 54782, so the service sets max_replicas_per_node: 1, and replicas beyond the number of eligible nodes stay pending.
  • Which class. A rerun uses the class of the original job, so set the resource_class of the job to debug to <namespace>/linux-default-ssh. To give an existing class SSH, copy three settings from the add-on file into that service: the environment variable, the host-mode port, and max_replicas_per_node: 1. Every replica of that class then needs its own node.
printf 'api:\n auth_token: %s\n' "$TOKEN" | docker secret create linux-default-ssh-token -
docker stack deploy -c deploy/runners.yaml -c deploy/ssh-rerun.yaml runners

Before you use it:

  • Firewall. Open inbound TCP 54782 on the nodes that run the class, only from the networks where your users connect, such as a VPN. Docker publishes the port with NAT rules that run before ufw and firewalld rules, so those rules do not restrict it. Filter in the DOCKER-USER chain or with a cloud security group, for example sudo iptables -I DOCKER-USER ! -s <VPN_RANGE> -p tcp --dport 54782 -j DROP (not tested here). Refer to Listening ports on a node.
  • SSH key. A user adds a public key in their CircleCI user settings, or, with a GitHub or Bitbucket organization, to their VCS account. Without a key, the Enable SSH step does not appear. Refer to Debug jobs with SSH rerun.
  • Concurrency. A rerun holds the runner for up to 2 hours after a user connects (1 hour on the Free plan), or 10 minutes if nobody does. It counts against the concurrency limit of your organization, and the replica takes no other job. A forgotten session blocks the node. Cancel the rerun in the web app or with the CLI when you finish: the container exits and Swarm starts a new one.
  • Security. The SSH user gets the privileges of the job user and can reach what the job reached. Anyone who can start a job on the class can rerun it with SSH, and only the user who reruns gets their keys added. In linux-default-ssh the job user keeps sudo, so the SSH user is root in the container, but it holds only the placeholder, because the class claims through the token proxy. Set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO to "false" to take root away. Keep the class for named projects and deploy contexts away from it (CircleCI-side controls).

On Windows, the SSH user must name the shell: ssh -p 54782 <HOST> -- powershell.exe. Open the port in Windows Defender Firewall as well.

Configuration reference

Variables in the stack files

Variable Value in the files Applies to Notes
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME "{{.Node.Hostname}}-<service>-{{.Task.Slot}}" Every service Required. Unique per replica
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE single-task, or continuous for persistent classes Every service single-task gives a new container for every job
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_IDLE_TIMEOUT 1h Single-task services An idle replica exits and Swarm replaces it. Do not set it in continuous mode
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR "false" on Linux, "true" on Windows Every service On Linux the runner user cannot remove files that the job user owns, so never set true there (Working directory cleanup)
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_LOGGING_FORMAT text Every service No color codes in logs
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_TIME Commented out, default 5h Every service If you lower it, set stop_grace_period to the same value plus 5 minutes
HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY Commented out Every service Jobs inherit them
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO "true" or "false" Linux "false" makes the class hardened
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_WORK_DIR, CIRCLECI_RUNNER_TASK_AGENT_DIRECTORY C:\cci\w, C:\cci\agent Windows Job working directory and task agent directory
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_INSTANCE_ID {{.Task.ID}} Windows Lets a job tell which container it ran in
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, GCM_INTERACTIVE, GIT_CONFIG_* 0, never, and core.longpaths=true Windows Stop Git prompts, and allow long paths
PATH The full Server Core path, then Git Windows stock services Replaces the image PATH, so the file spells it out

Refer to the machine runner 3 configuration reference for every other CIRCLECI_RUNNER_* variable. Environment variables override the config file.

Variables read by the Linux entrypoint

Variable Default Notes
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_WAIT 120 Seconds that the entrypoint waits for the link current of the distributor. Without it, the container exits with code 80
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_USER circleci The account that runs jobs. The entrypoint creates it with uid 2001 when the image has none
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO true false removes every sudo right of the job user and steps jobs down with setpriv --no-new-privs, which needs util-linux setpriv in the image. Any other value, or a missing setpriv, exits with code 80

The runner user is circleci-runner with uid 2000. It owns the secret file and has no sudo rights.

The entrypoint always sets CIRCLECI_RUNNER_COMMAND_PREFIX: ["sudo","-niHu","<job user>","--"], or a setpriv command when the image has no sudo, and always a setpriv --no-new-privs command in a hardened class. It keeps a value that you set for three more: CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR (default false), CIRCLECI_RUNNER_TASK_AGENT_DIRECTORY (default /var/lib/circleci-runner/agent, owned by the runner user) and CIRCLECI_RUNNER_WORK_DIR (default /var/opt/circleci/workdir, owned by the job user; keep a custom directory under /var/opt/circleci).

Arguments that you pass to the entrypoint replace the default command, machine --config /run/secrets/circleci_runner_config.yaml.

Variables read by the runner distributor

These are docker stack deploy variables. x-distributor-env in linux/stack/runners.yaml passes them to the runner-distributor service only. Refer to Upgrade the runner on Linux.

Variable Default Effect
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION An exact version, the newest that CI tests An exact version pins it. 3.1, 3 and current follow the manifest of CircleCI (the version policy)
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_MAJOR 3 The major version that current may adopt
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_CHECK_INTERVAL 24h How often a floating version looks at the manifest again: seconds, or a number with s, m, h, or d
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL https://circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com/circleci-runner Where manifest.json and the tarballs are, for example a mirror. It must be https://, unless a SHA-256 list is set
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 The tarball SHA-256 values of the pinned version A comma-separated list for an exact pin. manifest means no list: the hash of the manifest is trusted, which is weaker. A floating value ignores any list
MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_ALLOW_HTTP Not set true accepts an http:// download base without a SHA-256 list, for a lab

Stack keys on Windows

Not every key of a stack file reaches a Windows container.

Effect Keys
Used isolation, bind mounts of directories, npipe mounts, named volumes (a volume.subpath may be a relative directory symbolic link, but not a junction or an absolute link), Swarm configs with an absolute target, secrets without uid, gid, and mode, stop_grace_period, logging, entrypoint, environment with Swarm placeholders, labels, deploy.mode: global, deploy.placement, deploy.restart_policy, deploy.update_config, deploy.endpoint_mode, and deploy.resources.limits for cpus and memory
Scheduler only deploy.resources.reservations. The engine rejects a memory reservation, so Swarm never sends it
Rejected by the Windows engine deploy.resources.limits.pids and ulimits, so the files do not set them. A limits.cpus above the CPU count of the host is rejected too
No effect init, cap_drop, cap_add, read_only, tmpfs, and sysctls
Ignored by docker stack deploy on every platform security_opt, privileged, userns_mode, restart, and build

Three choices in the Windows files follow:

  • No hostname. A Windows computer name has at most 15 characters, and a templated hostname would give every container of a slot the same COMPUTERNAME. Without it, COMPUTERNAME is the container ID.
  • endpoint_mode: dnsrr. Nothing connects to a runner, so no virtual IP is needed.
  • Settings repeated per service. YAML merge keys do not merge deeply. The idle timeout is set for each service, because the persistent class must not have one, and windows-docker-build repeats the PATH with C:\docker appended.

The log driver is json-file with rotation. The local driver also works on Windows.

The secret

  • Linux, token proxy: secret <service>-token, target <service>-token, at /run/secrets/<service>-token in the proxy, uid 65534, gid 65534, mode 0400.
  • Linux, persistent runner and placeholder: secret <service>-token (a proxied class uses runner-placeholder-token), target circleci_runner_config.yaml, at /run/secrets/circleci_runner_config.yaml, uid 2000, gid 2000, mode 0400.
  • Windows: secret <service>-token, target circleci_runner_config.yaml, at C:\ProgramData\Docker\secrets\circleci_runner_config.yaml. Windows supports no owner or mode: administrators and SYSTEM only.

The content is api: and auth_token: <token> (the placeholder holds a made-up token). The proxy also accepts a bare token. The entrypoint passes --config <path> to the runner, and environment variables override the file.

Exit codes

Code Source Meaning
0 Runner A normal exit after a job or a runner drain. Swarm starts a new container
80 Entrypoint A prerequisite is missing: the link current does not exist after the wait, the runner does not match its SHA-256 record, the runner or a directory above it is not root-owned or is writable, the image has neither sudo nor setpriv (or, for a hardened class, no util-linux setpriv with --no-new-privs), MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO is invalid, or the entrypoint cannot remove every sudo right of the job user
80 Runner A configuration error: a missing or invalid name, an empty token, an unknown log level, or an invalid mode
1 Runner The config file is missing because the secret is not attached, the YAML does not parse, or a duration is malformed

Swarm restarts a container that exits with any code after 10 seconds. It never gives up and never backs off, so a configuration error repeats until you fix it (Troubleshooting).

item.title: Images
item.description:
The stack files run stock images and mount the runner into them, so the image of a class is the environment its jobs see. This repository publishes no class image. Its one image, the token proxy, holds the class tokens and is no environment for a job (The token proxy image). This page covers the stock images and how to bring your own on each OS.

Linux: stock images with the mounted runner

The statically linked runner lives in the per-node volume runner-bin, which the runner-distributor service fills. The stack mounts it read-only at /opt/machine-runner-swarm in every container, with current pointing to the active version. The entrypoint, a Swarm config mounted at /circleci-runner-entrypoint, starts as root, checks the runner against its SHA-256 record, prepares the users, and runs the runner as circleci-runner.

The image contains none of the runner, so a new runner version needs no image rebuild and no restart (The runner distributor on Linux, Upgrade the runner on Linux).

Service File Image
linux-default runners.yaml cimg/base:2026.10
linux-java classes-extra.yaml cimg/openjdk:21.0
linux-hardened classes-extra.yaml cimg/base:2026.10

What an image needs

Requirement Why
Linux, any C library The runner is statically linked. It runs unmodified in cimg/base, cimg/openjdk, Alpine, and UBI minimal
sudo, or util-linux setpriv Steps each job down to the job user. The hardened class (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO=false) needs util-linux setpriv with --no-new-privs, even when the image has sudo
setpriv or su Starts the runner as circleci-runner
useradd or adduser Creates circleci-runner, and the job user when the image has none
sed, grep, stat, install, getent, id, cut, tr, chmod, env, sha256sum, readlink, sleep Used by the entrypoint. BusyBox and coreutils both provide them
wget or curl, tar, awk, mktemp, mv, chown Only for a microVM class, whose entrypoint downloads the runner

The cimg images have everything. Alpine has only the BusyBox su, and UBI minimal has neither sudo nor setpriv. The tests run the entrypoint in cimg/base, cimg/openjdk, Alpine 3 (with sudo and with setpriv), and UBI 9 minimal. Add missing packages in a derived image:

Base Add
Debian and Ubuntu apt-get install sudo
Alpine apk add sudo setpriv
UBI minimal microdnf install sudo util-linux (util-linux-core is not enough)

The entrypoint exits with code 80 and names the missing packages. The end-to-end CI jobs run real jobs through the sudo path (default class) and the setpriv --no-new-privs path (hardened class).

The job user is circleci by default. Set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_USER to another existing account. If the account does not exist, the entrypoint creates it with uid 2001, with passwordless sudo while MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO is true and the image has sudo. The image environment (PATH, JAVA_HOME, LANG, proxy variables) reaches the jobs. The runner token does not.

Pin the image

Tags such as 21.0 move when the publisher rebuilds the image. Pin production services by digest and update them on a schedule:

image: cimg/base:2026.10@sha256:<DIGEST>
docker buildx imagetools inspect cimg/base:2026.10

Linux: bring your own image

Build an image when jobs need tools that you do not want to install in every job. This is also how a hardened class gets tools, because jobs there have no sudo.

linux/images/example/Dockerfile starts from a cimg image and adds postgresql-client. Copy it and replace the packages.

docker build -t registry.example.com/ci/linux-pg:1 linux/images/example
docker push registry.example.com/ci/linux-pg:1

Then set the image of a service in your stack file:

image: registry.example.com/ci/linux-pg:1

Every node that runs the service must be able to pull the image (Registry needs). Rebuild when the base changes, for example once a month.

The Dockerfile adds tools and nothing of the runner. Its USER circleci only affects a plain docker run: the stack starts the container as root so that the entrypoint can create users.

Windows: stock Server Core with mounts

The default Windows service runs the unmodified Microsoft Server Core image, for example mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022. Two read-only mounts of the per-node volume runner-bin, which runner-distributor-windows fills, add what the runner needs:

Volume path (volume.subpath) Container path Content
current C:\machine-runner-swarm bin\circleci-runner.exe, the record SHA256, and VERSION
git\current C:\Program Files\Git Portable Git for Windows: git, bash, sh, tar, gzip, ssh

current and git\current are relative directory symbolic links, to versions\<version> and to the pinned Git, which the distributor moves. Docker resolves a link when it creates a container, so a new runner version reaches the next container only, and a running job keeps its version. Docker refuses a junction or an absolute link in a subpath (Upgrade the runner on Windows).

The runner is the main process: the service sets entrypoint to C:\machine-runner-swarm\bin\circleci-runner.exe machine --config C:\ProgramData\Docker\secrets\circleci_runner_config.yaml. It also sets the full PATH, because a PATH in the service environment replaces the one of the image. Git for Windows comes after the Windows directories, so the Windows find, sort, and tar stay first.

The Git mount is read-only, so the service sets Git options through the environment: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0, and GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 enable core.longpaths, and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and GCM_INTERACTIVE=never stop prompts that nothing in a container can answer.

Pin the image with a digest, and redeploy when Microsoft republishes the tag (each Patch Tuesday).

docker buildx imagetools inspect mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022

Nano Server is not supported. Windows images must match the host build (Image tags and host builds).

Windows: bring your own image

Add tools in an image on top of stock Server Core. The host still provides the runner and Git through the mounts, and the stack file still sets entrypoint and the full PATH, so add the directory of your tool to that PATH.

windows/images/example/Dockerfile adds Node.js from the official zip, pinned by version and SHA-256. Copy it and swap the tool, keeping the pattern:

  1. Start FROM the stock Server Core image of your host’s tag.
  2. Download a pinned release, and verify its SHA-256 checksum before you use it.
  3. Install the tool in a fixed directory, and add that directory to the PATH of the service in windows\stack\custom-image.yaml.
  4. Check that the tool runs. Leave USER alone: the runner needs ContainerAdministrator, which creates symbolic links for the task agent.

Do not put PsExec64.exe on the PATH of the image or of the service: the task agent would switch to a desktop wrapper that containers cannot run.

Build the example from the root of the repository (the build context is the windows directory):

docker build -f windows/images/example/Dockerfile --build-arg WINDOWS_TAG=ltsc2022 -t machine-runner-swarm-windows-example:ltsc2022 windows

Push the result to a registry that every Windows node can pull from, because Swarm does not share local images. Then set the image of the windows-custom service in the add-on stack file windows\stack\custom-image.yaml, create the resource class and the secret windows-custom-token, and deploy with -c windows\stack\runners.yaml -c windows\stack\custom-image.yaml. The file examples/windows-custom-image.yml has a job on that class. Rebuild when the base image or a tool changes.

A stop of a busy Windows container kills its job after about 5 seconds (Stop a busy Windows container).

Private certificate authorities

The runner, its task agent, and the job steps read the certificate store of the image of their class. To trust a private authority (an inspecting proxy, your CircleCI server, a private registry, or a package host), put it in an image of your own. The stack files need no change. This repository does not test it.

On Linux, add the certificate to the system store, in a Dockerfile on top of your image:

FROM cimg/base:2026.10@sha256:<DIGEST>
USER root
COPY my-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/my-ca.crt
RUN update-ca-certificates
USER circleci

On Windows, add it to the Root store on top of stock Server Core. Go reads the Windows certificate store, so the runner needs the authority there:

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022
COPY my-ca.cer C:/ca/my-ca.cer
RUN certutil -addstore -f Root C:\ca\my-ca.cer

Some tools keep their own bundle: set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS for Node.js, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE for Python requests, and the keystore of Java in the image too. On Unix, SSL_CERT_FILE replaces the roots of a Go program instead of adding to them, so point it at a bundle with the public roots and yours.

The image does not reach the other components that make TLS calls: the Docker engine of the node (image pulls), the token proxy, and the two runner distributors. Proxies and certificate authorities, component by component lists what each needs, and what does not work.

item.title: Migrate from Docker Compose
item.description:
Warning

This repository no longer ships the Docker Compose setup. The files docker-compose.yml, base-image/, convenience-image/, and machine-image/ were removed in the Swarm rewrite, and the change is marked [BREAKING] in the changelog. Find the old files with git log -- docker-compose.yml.

The old setup restarted the same container after each job, so jobs did not get a clean environment. The Swarm stack creates a new container for every job (Why not plain Docker Compose?). This page covers Linux hosts, which the old setup supported. Your job configs, resource classes and tokens can stay.

What changed

Old setup Swarm stack
Services base, convenience, and machine in docker-compose.yml One service for each resource class in linux/stack/runners.yaml. The continuous runner is linux/stack/persistent.yaml
restart: unless-stopped, which restarts the same container restart_policy: condition: any, which creates a new container
Token in a .env file as CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_AUTH_TOKEN, visible in docker inspect Swarm secret <service>-token, which holds a runner config file
The same CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME for every replica {{.Node.Hostname}}-<service>-{{.Task.Slot}}, unique for each replica
Dockerfiles that build the runner into an image A stock image, with the runner mounted from the volume runner-bin (Images)
CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE and CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR in the service environment The same variables, in the stack file. Cleanup is "false" on Linux

Migrate

  1. Name the classes. A Swarm service must have the name of its resource class. To keep your classes and tokens, name each service after the class it replaces, for example base. For new classes, create them.

  2. Prepare the host. Docker Engine is already there. Start Swarm and install nothing else: the runner-distributor service installs the runner on every node (Start Swarm).

  3. Create the secrets. Use the token of each class, the value of CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_AUTH_TOKEN in your old .env file (Create the secrets).

  4. Choose the images. The old convenience service maps to cimg/base or another cimg image, and base to a stock image with your tools. Move extra tools from your Dockerfiles into a derived image (Linux: bring your own image).

  5. Edit the stack file. Rename or copy the services, set your old replica counts, and keep only what you need. The old machine service becomes linux/stack/persistent.yaml (Resource Classes).

  6. Deploy next to the old setup. Both can run at once, because the runner names differ. Check that the new runners show up in the inventory. If a new service keeps a class whose old runners are busy, the token proxy sees running tasks at its first start, cannot tell whose they are, and refuses the present runners until their idle timeout, or until you run the command below once the old runners are idle. New classes avoid this (Restart the proxy).

    docker service update --force --update-parallelism 0 runners_<SERVICE>

  7. Stop the old setup. When the old runners are idle, run docker compose down in the old directory. A running job is stopped after the Compose grace period, so wait for a quiet period.

  8. Clean up. Delete the old .env files, which hold tokens in clear text. If you created new classes, delete the old tokens and classes in CircleCI.

Behavior to expect

  • Runner updates. The runner is an exact pin by default: the newest version this repository’s CI tests, bumped by each release of this repository. Set 3.1, 3 or current to follow CircleCI’s manifest (Upgrade the runner on Linux).
  • Sudo. The default classes keep passwordless sudo, as the old images did. The hardened class removes it (Concepts).
  • Fixed replicas. The stack does not scale by itself, and a node that dies is not replaced (Capacity and concurrency).
  • Startup time. A new container starts for every job, so a job waits about 10 seconds longer for the next claim, plus the task agent download. Add replicas for busy classes.
  • Swarm on one host. Swarm mode is required even on a single host. The helper and the install page start it on the loopback address, so nothing is exposed.
  • Working directory. The runner no longer removes the working directory on Linux, because it runs as another user than the jobs. A new container for every job leaves nothing behind, but a persistent class (the old machine service) keeps files between jobs, so start its jobs with a cleanup step (Working directory cleanup).

item.title: Quickstart on Windows Server
item.description:
Go from nothing to a first job on one Windows Server node in five steps. Nothing is built or installed on the host: the stack uses the stock Server Core image, and a service of the stack installs the runner and Git.

Note

This is a CircleCI Labs project, not supported by CircleCI support. It is a 0.x release: read the release notes before you upgrade. What is tested says how it is checked. One token proxy runs on a manager, so while it is down no new job starts. This page sets up one host that runs the proxy and the jobs together: use it for a trial.

Before you start

  • A Windows Server 2022 or 2025 host (amd64, not a domain controller) with a clock on NTP and outbound HTTPS (what needs internet).
  • Docker Engine and CLI 28.0 or later in Windows-container mode, and the Windows Containers feature (Prerequisites shows how to install both). The first pull of the Server Core image is about 2.2 GB.
  • The CircleCI CLI 1.4.0 or later, on your workstation or on the host.
  • An organization admin who accepted the CircleCI Runner Terms.
  • A runner namespace. If your organization has none, create one with circleci namespace create <NAMESPACE> --org <ORG>.
  • An elevated Windows PowerShell 5.1 session on the host.

Replace <NAMESPACE> with your runner namespace, and <ORG> with your organization slug such as gh/my-org, or its UUID.

Steps

  1. Create a resource class and a token. The command prints the token once: keep it for step 3.

    circleci auth login
circleci runner resource-class create <NAMESPACE>/windows-default --org <ORG> --generate-token

  2. On the host, download the latest release. To verify the release signature first, see Install on Windows Server > Verify a release.

    $uri = (Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri 'https://github.com/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/releases/latest').BaseResponse.ResponseUri.AbsoluteUri
$version = $uri -replace '^.*/v', ''
$zip = "machine-runner-swarm-$version.zip"
Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "https://github.com/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/releases/download/v$version/$zip" -OutFile $zip
Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $zip -DestinationPath .
cd "machine-runner-swarm-$version"

  3. Pull the base image, then run the helper. Pull first: the network of the host drops for a few seconds after docker swarm init. The helper creates the Swarm, labels the node, asks for the token from step 1 (hidden input), creates the secrets, and deploys the stack. Use the IPv4 address of the host.

    docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022
    .\windows\Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm -AdvertiseAddr <HOST_IPV4_ADDRESS> -Class windows-default -Deploy

  4. Check the stack. docker stack deploy does not wait, and the first start downloads the runner, so the replicas need a few minutes. Early runner tasks fail until the download ends, and Swarm restarts them.

    docker stack services runners
circleci runner instance list --org <ORG> --resource-class <NAMESPACE>/windows-default

    The stack is up when runners_windows-default shows 2/2 and the CLI lists an instance with the status online. If a replica stays Pending, the host is too small: each replica reserves 2 CPUs and 4 GB, so set a lower deploy.replicas (Size the limits, A task stays pending). docker service logs runners_runner-distributor-windows shows the install.

  5. Run a job. Save this as .circleci/config.yml in a project of your organization, replace my-namespace with your namespace, then commit and push. The file examples/windows-job.yml has more steps.

    version: 2.1

jobs:
 hello:
 machine: true
 resource_class: my-namespace/windows-default
 steps:
 - run: echo "computer $COMPUTERNAME, instance $MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_INSTANCE_ID"

workflows:
 hello:
 jobs:
 - hello

    Run the workflow twice. The two runs print different values, because Swarm starts a new container for each job.

What differs from Linux

  • A job runs as an administrator. The runner container holds a placeholder, and the class token stays in the token proxy, except in the windows-persistent class (Token model on each OS).
  • Stopping a busy container, for an update, a scale-down or a drain, kills its job after about 5 seconds. Change a class while it is idle (Stop a busy Windows container).

Next

  • Install on Windows Server: every step by hand, release verification, and upgrades. Before production, copy windows\stack to a directory of your own and deploy that copy (Review the stack files).
  • Concepts: services as resource classes, the token proxy, and the job lifecycle.
  • Images: add your own tools on top of Server Core.
  • Security: the token model and BitLocker.
  • Operations: upgrade, rotate tokens, and run the cluster.

item.title: Releasing
item.description:
This page is for maintainers. A CircleCI job makes every release when a change is merged to main. Nobody tags a release by hand, edits a changelog, or pushes a release commit. The job creates the tag through the GitHub API.

  • Version and notes rules: cliff.toml
  • The job: release in the ci workflow of .circleci/continue.yml, and ci/release.sh
  • How users check a release: Verify a release

Make a release

  1. Bump the runner pin in a commit before the release (Bump the runner version), for example feat(runner): pin <VERSION> by default.

  2. Preview the next version and its notes in a clone with the tags:

    git cliff --bumped-version
git cliff --unreleased --tag "$(git cliff --bumped-version)" --strip header

  3. Merge the pull request to main. The pipeline runs every test, then the release job publishes.

  4. If a job fails, fix it and use Rerun workflow from failed in CircleCI.

  5. Check the release:

    gh release view <TAG> --repo CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm

    Then verify the bundle and the image, including the ref, as a user does (Verify a release).

A push with only docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor or build commits makes no release. The job ends green with Nothing to release since vX.Y.Z.

What happens on merge

  1. The setup phase (.circleci/config.yml) passes release: true when the branch is main, both e2e tokens are present, and a commit of the push would make a release (cliff.toml). That switches on every suite, full-suite, e2e-linux, e2e-windows and strict. Otherwise it passes release: false, because a release must wait for every test.
  2. The release job requires every other job of the ci workflow except three optional ones. If one fails, nothing is released.
  3. The job runs in the serial group <project slug>/release. When a newer pipeline’s release job waits in the group, the older one skips and the newer one releases both changes.
  4. ci/release.sh checks the Swarm config names (Swarm config names) and the runner pin, computes the version and notes, pins the pipeline’s token proxy image digest in the bundle’s stack files, builds the bundles, signs SHA256SUMS and verifies the signature. It then verifies the image signature, gives the image its release tags, and creates the GitHub release, which creates the tag.
  5. When the job publishes, it records two Deploys in CircleCI: machine-runner-swarm in github-releases (version the tag), and token-proxy-image in docker-hub (version X.Y.Z). A deploy ends as SUCCESS, or FAILED when a step fails (Deploys).

A release needs the image of its commit. proxy-image-publish of the same pipeline pushes it as sha-<12 characters>, and the release requires that job. Without DOCKERHUB_USERNAME and DOCKERHUB_TOKEN in the context scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub (Docker Hub context), a pipeline that is not the production main stays green and publishes nothing: the release job stores the bundle as an artifact and creates no GitHub release. On the production main the same gap fails the jobs (Publishing fails closed on main).

Other branches and tag pipelines never release. A push to main that changes only documentation has no e2e and no release job, unless a commit would make a release, such as fix(docs): (Documentation-only changes).

Add a new job to requires of the release job in .circleci/continue.yml. lint-circleci compiles the workflow and fails when a job is missing. Its $optional list is the only exception: linux-mixed-arch (the emulated mixed-architecture test), proxy-image-edge (moves the edge tag after the tests) and docs-site-comment (posts the preview address on a pull request).

Versions

The project follows Semantic Versioning and starts at 0.x. Tags are vX.Y.Z. git-cliff computes the next version from the Conventional Commits since the last tag. cliff.toml sets initial_tag = "v0.1.0" for a repository with no tag.

Commits since the last release Next version while 0.x
A breaking change: type!: or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer Minor, for example 0.2.3 to 0.3.0
feat Minor
fix, perf, revert Patch
Only docs, test, ci, chore, style, refactor or build No release
Not a Conventional Commit, such as a GitHub “Merge pull request” commit Ignored

A breaking change never raises the major number: 1.0.0 is a decision for people. To allow it, set breaking_always_bump_major = true and features_always_bump_minor = false in the [bump] section of cliff.toml. The next breaking change then makes 1.0.0.

Release notes

git-cliff writes the notes for the GitHub release: breaking changes first, then features, bug fixes, performance changes and reverts. The (#123) that GitHub adds to a squash merge title links to the pull request, and an entry without one links to its commit. CHANGELOG.md in the repository only points to GitHub Releases. The release bundle holds a generated CHANGELOG.md with every release.

What a release contains

Asset Content
machine-runner-swarm-<version>.tar.gz README.md, LICENSE, SECURITY.md, VERSION, the generated CHANGELOG.md, docs/, examples/, linux/ and windows/
machine-runner-swarm-<version>.zip The same files, for Windows users
SHA256SUMS The SHA-256 checksum of both bundles
SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json The cosign bundle: signature, certificate and transparency log entry

The bundles come from git archive, so only tracked files ship. They leave out linux/tests/, windows/tests/, docs/ci.md, docs/releasing.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ci/, .circleci/, proxy/ and site/. ci/bundle-links.py turns every link from a shipped page to a left-out file into a link to that file on GitHub at the release tag (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/vX.Y.Z/...), and stops the release when a link is dead in the repository too. ci/tests/bundle-links.sh tests it in lint-circleci.

The token proxy image

The token proxy is a published image, ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy on Docker Hub, not a release asset. One tag is a manifest list for linux/amd64, arm64, ppc64le and s390x, and Windows Server 2022 and 2025 (windows/amd64). There is no windows/arm64 image (install-windows.md).

Event Tags pushed
A pull request or a branch None: built and tested only
A merge to main sha-<12 characters of the commit>, by proxy-image-publish
The same merge, after the four linux-swarm jobs and every e2e group pass edge, by proxy-image-edge, the last job of the pipeline. It stays put when a newer commit is on main
A release (ci/release.sh) X.Y.Z (immutable), X.Y, X and latest, on the digest of that commit’s sha-<12> image. Nothing is rebuilt

The stack files of a checkout default to latest, so only the release job changes what a checkout deploys, and it runs after every test. edge is the newest tested commit, and sha-<12> is one commit that nothing has tested yet. Neither is a default. Before the first release, set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE to a sha-<12> or edge tag, or use a release bundle.

X.Y.Z never moves: a release that finds it on another digest stops. X.Y, X and latest move only when the release is the newest of its minor line, its major line and overall. Three helper tags (sha-<12>-linux, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2022, sha-<12>-windows-ltsc2025) hold parts of the manifest list: do not pull them.

The pipeline builds and runs each image (ci/proxy-image.sh, ci/Build-ProxyImage.ps1, jobs in CI/CD). On main (the pipeline parameter publish), proxy-image-publish joins the helper images with crane index append, tags the list sha-<12>, checks every platform, and signs every digest keyless with the CircleCI OIDC token. The release job pins the digest in the bundle’s stack files (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE:-ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:<version>@sha256:<digest>, in place of :latest), checks the signature, and adds the four release tags.

A checkout keeps latest, which Renovate does not manage. A release bundle carries its own digest, and it is the documented way to install. Users verify the image with cosign (Verify the token proxy image) and must check that the certificate names refs/heads/main (How the signature works).

Bump the runner version

The stack files pin one exact runner version by default: MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION: ${MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION:-3.1.13} in the distributor settings of linux/stack/runners.yaml and windows/stack/runners.yaml, and in x-env of linux/stack/microvm.yaml. It is the newest version that CI tests (STACK_RUNNER_PIN in linux/tests/lib.sh), so a release carries the pin that CI tested. Bump it in a commit before each release:

  1. Pick the newest version in the manifest that has linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x and windows amd64, arm64. List versions with jq -r '.releases | keys[]' manifest.json and check .releases["<version>"]. Read the runner changelog.
  2. In one commit, change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION in all three stack files. Change the default of MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 to the tarball SHA-256 values of that version (from the release’s checksums.txt or the manifest), comma-separated: linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le, s390x in linux/stack/runners.yaml and linux/stack/microvm.yaml, and windows amd64, arm64 in windows/stack/runners.yaml.
  3. Commit it as feat(runner): pin 3.1.14 by default for a new minor or patch that users should get, or fix(runner): ... for a fix, so that git-cliff makes a release. Let CI run.
  4. Update the docs examples (docs/operations.md uses 3.1.12 and 3.1.13) only when you want them to move.

The version must be equal in every file: linux/tests/stack-config.sh fails when it differs. The release job (check_runner_pin in ci/release.sh) fails when the version is not in the manifest for every platform, or when a default SHA-256 list does not match the manifest. A user gets the new runner by deploying the new release. A user who sets the variable keeps what they set.

How the signature works

The job gets an OIDC token with circleci run oidc get --claims '{"aud":"sigstore"}' --root-issuer. The audience sigstore and the issuer https://oidc.circleci.com are what the public Sigstore certificate authority (Fulcio) accepts for CircleCI. cosign sign-blob swaps the token for a short-lived certificate, signs SHA256SUMS and records the signature in the public Rekor log. No key is kept.

The certificate identity is https://circleci.com/api/v2/projects/<project-id>/pipeline-definitions/<pipeline-definition-id>. It is the same for every branch, and a job of any branch can get an OIDC token with no context, so the identity alone does not prove that main signed. The source repository ref does: the certificate extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.14, which Fulcio fills from the vcs-ref claim. It is refs/heads/main for a release and refs/heads/<branch> for any other branch.

cosign has flags for the GitHub extensions only, so ci/tools.sh reads the certificate itself (signed_only_on, tested by ci/tests/signature-ref.sh):

  • ci/release.sh runs cosign verify-blob on SHA256SUMS, then checks that the certificate names refs/heads/main. The job stops if it does not.
  • ci/proxy-image.sh does the same for every digest of the token proxy image, right after signing and again in the release job before the release tags. It reads every signature of the digest (cosign download signature): one signature of a feature branch next to one of main fails the check.

To check the ref by hand, after cosign verify-blob printed Verified OK, run this. The hex string is the OID followed by refs/heads/main, so it matches the whole value:

jq -r '.verificationMaterial | (.certificate // .x509CertificateChain.certificates[0]).rawBytes' SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json | base64 -d \
 | od -An -v -tx1 | tr -d ' \n' | grep -Eq '^([0-9a-f]{2})*2b0601040183bf30010e0411(0c|13)0f726566732f68656164732f6d61696e' \
 && echo "signed for refs/heads/main" || echo "NOT signed for refs/heads/main: do not use this release"

CircleCI documents OIDC tokens for jobs that use a context. In a test on 2026-10-13, circleci run oidc get also worked in a job without one, which is why the ref and not the identity decides.

Where the signature of the image is stored, and the tries

cosign 3.1.3 stores an image signature as a Sigstore bundle, pushed as an OCI 1.1 referrer of the signed digest. cosign verify and cosign download signature fall back to the older sha256-<hex>.sig tag only when they find no referrer (the source of no signatures found). ci/proxy-image.sh pins the format with --new-bundle-format=true on both commands (the variable cosign_storage). The flag is the default of 3.1.3 and deprecated: when a cosign version drops it, the rehearsal of the pull request that updates cosign fails, and main does not.

Docker Hub probably does not list a referrer at once: the first run on main failed with no signatures found right after cosign sign. verify_signature therefore tries up to six times, waiting 5, 10, 15, 25 and 35 seconds between tries (SIGN_VERIFY_DELAYS sets the waits). Every check stays whole in every try: identity, issuer, and the ref refs/heads/main on every signature. A signature that names another ref fails at once. After the last failed try, the job prints cosign tree of the digest and the repository tags that start with sha256-.

The signing rehearsal

Signing runs for real on main only, so a failure would first show on a merge and leave sha-<12> tags with no release. The job signing-rehearsal runs the same code in every pipeline that is not documentation-only, on any branch, with no context and no secret (ci/proxy-image.sh rehearse):

  1. It pushes a throwaway image to a registry:2 container of the job at localhost:5000.
  2. It signs the image against the real Fulcio and Rekor (a brief failure is tried again, three times) and verifies it with verify_signature, the function that main uses, for the ref refs/heads/<branch of the pipeline>.
  3. It checks that the same signature is refused for another ref, so a check that stopped looking at the ref turns the pipeline red.

Each rehearsal adds an entry to the public Rekor log with the project, branch and commit. The release requires the job.

Enable publishing

Until you do this, the release job runs every step except the last and stays green on a project with no e2e tokens. It prints publishing skipped: GITHUB_TOKEN is not set in context scalable-machine-runner-release and keeps the version, notes, bundles and signature as job artifacts. On the production main (both e2e tokens present) it fails with the same message.

  1. Create a fine-grained personal access token with the resource owner CircleCI-Labs, only this repository, and the repository permission Contents: Read and write. Nothing else is needed, because gh release create makes the tag and the release. The token expires, so note the date to rotate it. A GitHub App installation token expires after one hour, so it does not fit a context variable.

  2. In the CircleCI organization settings, create the context scalable-machine-runner-release and add the variable GITHUB_TOKEN with the token.

  3. Restrict the context to this project, and add an expression restriction so that only pipelines of main can use it, not an SSH rerun that could print the token and not an API pipeline (which can name any branch and may bring its own config):

    pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")

    With the CLI, where <PROJECT_ID> is 7bbdbb66-6ba8-4f6c-982e-d4fb401ec257:

    circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-release --org <ORG> --type project --value <PROJECT_ID>
circleci context restriction create scalable-machine-runner-release --org <ORG> --type expression \
 --value 'pipeline.git.branch == "main" and not job.ssh.enabled and not (pipeline.config_source starts-with "api")'

    In the organization’s advanced settings, leave pipelines with an unversioned config off.

  4. In the project settings (Advanced), keep Build forked pull requests and Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests off.

  5. Protect main with the ruleset in A ruleset for main: a pull request required, no force push, no bypass, and the check ci. Whoever can change .circleci/ or ci/release.sh on main controls what runs with the token. What the release trust depends on lists every setting that the signature relies on.

The docs site, its pull request comment and the weekly security scan have their own contexts (What a maintainer creates once). Do not reuse this token for them: it can publish releases. The next release run on main publishes. To check before then, read the release job log for publishing skipped.

What the release trust depends on

A valid signature says one thing: a job of this CircleCI project, from the pipeline definition of this repository, ran on refs/heads/main of this repository. The claim holds only as far as the settings below hold. They are settings of GitHub, CircleCI and Docker Hub, not of the repository, so no file can enforce or show them, and ci/release.sh does not check them. The maintainers have set all of them for v0.1.0. Check the settings says how to read them back.

The main-only expression below is the one in Enable publishing step 3. Every context also has a project restriction (this project).

Setting Where It must say Without it
Ruleset of main GitHub repository Require a pull request. Block force pushes. Restrict deletions. No bypass list. Required status check: ci (A ruleset for main) A writer could push a change of .circleci/ or ci/release.sh to main, and it would be signed
Ruleset of smr-swarm/** GitHub repository Restrict creations and updates, maintainers alone on the bypass list (The e2e context and smr-swarm/*) A writer could print the e2e runner tokens in a public log from an smr-swarm/<name> branch
Context scalable-machine-runner-release CircleCI organization project and the main-only expression Another branch, an SSH rerun or an API pipeline could read the token
Context scalable-machine-runner-dockerhub CircleCI organization The same two restrictions (The Docker Hub context) A branch could push the image that the stack files name
Context scalable-machine-runner-docs CircleCI organization The same two restrictions A branch could read a token that can write to the repository
Context scalable-machine-runner-e2e CircleCI organization project, and the main-only expression with (pipeline.git.branch == "main" or pipeline.git.branch starts-with "smr-swarm/") in place of the branch test A branch could read the e2e runner tokens
Context scalable-machine-runner-pr-comments CircleCI organization project, and the main-only expression without the branch test. Any branch pusher can read it, so its token has the least permission (Docs site previews) An SSH rerun or an API pipeline could read it
Project settings CircleCI project and organization Build forked pull requests, Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests, Auto-cancel redundant workflows, SSH reruns and pipelines with an unversioned config: all off (Secrets and public logs) A fork or an API pipeline could run a config of its own
Tokens GitHub, Docker Hub Release and docs tokens: fine-grained, this repository only, Contents: Read and write. Comment token: Issues: Read and write, of a bot account. Docker Hub token: read and write on ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy only, from an account with two-factor authentication (What each job can see) A leaked token would reach more than the job that needs it

Two things are not covered. The signature does not say that anyone reviewed the change (the ruleset sets the number of reviews, and .github/CODEOWNERS asks the same people for every path), and it says nothing about main before the ruleset existed.

Check the settings

Read the GitHub settings back with the API. The first command lists the rules that apply to main (it must include pull_request, non_fast_forward, deletion and required_status_checks). The second and third show the bypass list of a ruleset, which must be empty for main:

gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rules/branches/main --jq '.[].type'
gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rulesets --jq '.[] | "\(.id) \(.name) \(.enforcement)"'
gh api repos/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/rulesets/<ID> --jq '{conditions, bypass_actors, rules: [.rules[].type]}'

The ruleset of smr-swarm/** must show creation and update. The CLI cannot list context restrictions, so read them from the API for each of the five contexts and compare them with the table. Find a context id with circleci context list --org <ORG>:

curl -s --header "circle-token: ${CIRCLECI_TOKEN}" https://circleci.com/api/v2/context/<CONTEXT_ID>/restrictions

The project settings are in the web app (Project Settings, then Advanced), and the Docker Hub token scope is in the account’s security settings. Keep the output with the release pull request.

Rotate the e2e runner tokens

Rotate both e2e runner tokens when one may have leaked, and when someone who could read them leaves the project. For each class, create a new token, store it in the context, run one pipeline on main and check that both e2e groups pass, then delete the old token. circleci context secret set prompts for the value in a terminal, so the token stays out of the shell history:

circleci runner token create cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-linux --nickname ci-YYYYMM
circleci context secret set scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org <ORG> --name E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_LINUX
circleci runner token create cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-windows --nickname ci-YYYYMM
circleci context secret set scalable-machine-runner-e2e --org <ORG> --name E2E_RUNNER_TOKEN_WINDOWS
circleci runner token list --resource-class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-linux
circleci runner token list --resource-class cci-labs/scalable-machine-runner-e2e-windows
circleci runner token delete <OLD_TOKEN_ID>

Merge method

The notes come from the commits on main, so the merge method decides what they show.

  • Merge commit or rebase and merge. Every commit of the pull request gets its own entry, so use it for small, atomic Conventional Commits (Commit messages). The GitHub merge commit is not a Conventional Commit, so the notes ignore it.
  • Squash and merge. The pull request becomes one commit with its title as the message, and one entry that links to the pull request. Write the title as a Conventional Commit. A pull request that mixes a feat and a fix loses one of them.

Mark a breaking change with ! or a BREAKING CHANGE: footer, in a commit message or in the title of a squashed pull request.

Tag pipelines

The project uses the GitHub OAuth integration (project slug gh/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm), which has no trigger settings: CircleCI starts a pipeline for every push that GitHub reports, so the tag that the release creates starts one. In it, pipeline.git.tag is the tag, and pipeline.git.branch and CIRCLE_BRANCH are empty.

That pipeline cannot release and runs no job. CircleCI runs no job for a tag unless the job has a tag filter, and no job in .circleci/ has one. To build for tags, give a job a tag filter on purpose, and keep the release context out of that job.

Rerun and recovery

Rerunning is safe. Before it publishes, the job looks for a release tag at its commit, and it never creates a second release. Rerunning a pipeline from before a later release releases nothing.

Situation What to do
The release job failed before it published Rerun the job. It computes the same version
An asset of an existing release is missing Rerun the job. It uploads all assets again with --clobber
A tag exists at another commit Stop. Somebody created vX.Y.Z by hand, or an older release was moved. Compare git rev-parse vX.Y.Z with the commit of the pipeline. Delete the wrong tag and release with gh release delete vX.Y.Z --cleanup-tag, then rerun the job
This commit is already part of vX.Y.Z A later commit was already released. The job did nothing
The release job shows as skipped A newer pipeline waits for the release lock and will release this change too
The Deploys view shows FAILED Read the reason there, fix the cause and rerun the job. It records a new deploy of the same version
gh fails with 401 or 403 The token expired or lost its permission. Replace GITHUB_TOKEN in the context and rerun the job
A release is wrong Prefer a new release that fixes it. If you delete a release and its tag, the next run makes the same version again

Pinned tools

ci/release.sh install-tools installs the tools of the job. Each download is checked against a SHA-256 value in the script (cosign and crane are in ci/tools.sh), and the job image is pinned by digest. Each tool has its version and SHA-256 value in two variables, with a # renovate: comment above the version.

Tool Version Source of the SHA-256 value
git-cliff 2.14.2 The .sha512 file of the release, and a local sha256sum
cosign 3.1.3 cosign_checksums.txt of the release
crane 0.22.1 checksums.txt of the release (the Linux x86_64 archive)
gh 2.102.0 gh_2.102.0_checksums.txt of the release
Go 1.27.2 The download page of go.dev, next to the archive
cimg/base 2026.10 The digest in .circleci/continue.yml

Renovate opens a pull request that changes the version only. It has the label checksum and fails on the checksum until you replace the SHA-256 value in the same branch. To update a tool by hand, change its version and SHA-256 value together in install_tools (cosign and crane: in ci/tools.sh), then follow Try it locally. To update the job image, follow Pinned versions. A Renovate pull request for Go also moves the golang and cimg/go images, so the release proxy binaries use the same Go as proxy-test.

Try it locally

Everything except publishing and signing runs on an x86_64 Linux workstation. The first command installs git-cliff, cosign, crane and gh into ~/.local/bin, and Go into ~/.local/go. The second writes the files to /tmp/release and signs and publishes nothing.

ci/release.sh install-tools
RELEASE_SKIP_SIGN=1 ci/release.sh

To check that the release job requires every job of the workflow, as lint-circleci does, compile the config with every parameter on and read the release entry of workflows.ci.jobs:

circleci config process .circleci/continue.yml \
 --pipeline-parameters '{full-suite: true, e2e-linux: true, e2e-windows: true, release: true, publish: true}'

item.title: Troubleshooting
item.description:
Each entry gives the symptom, the cause and the fix. Start with the task state and the runner output:

docker stack ps runners --no-trunc
docker service logs --tail 100 runners_<SERVICE>

For CircleCI guidance shared by all runners, refer to Troubleshoot self-hosted runner.

General

A task stays pending

Symptom: the ERROR column of docker service ps --no-trunc runners_<service> shows no suitable node.

Cause. No node satisfies the task.

  • scheduling constraints not satisfied on N nodes: a label is missing, the OS or architecture differs, or the service needs a worker and the label sits on a manager.
  • insufficient resources on N nodes: the reservations exceed what the matching nodes have free. Reservations equal the limits, so extra replicas wait on purpose.
  • max replicas per node: the SSH add-on runs one replica on each node, because a node has one host-mode port 54782.

Fix. Compare the constraints of the service with the labels of the nodes. Then add the label (docker node update --label-add), add nodes, lower replicas, or lower the reservations (Labels and constraints).

docker service inspect --format '{{ json .Spec.TaskTemplate.Placement }}' runners_<SERVICE>
docker node inspect --format '{{ .Description.Hostname }} {{ .Spec.Labels }}' $(docker node ls -q)

The container restarts every 10 seconds

Symptom: docker service ps lists many tasks of one slot, each with task: non-zero exit (80) or (1), started 10 to 12 seconds apart.

Cause. The runner or the entrypoint exits at start-up on a configuration error. Swarm restarts the container after 10 seconds and never gives up, so the loop runs until you fix the cause. The stack sets no max_attempts, because the runner would then never recover by itself: alert on exit code 80 instead. The log line names the problem:

Log text Cause
api.auth_token must be set The secret has an empty token, or the wrong structure
runner.name must be set CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME is missing
runner.name must contain only letters, numbers, .()_-, and spaces Other characters, or more than 64 (long hostname or class name)
--runner.mode must be one of "continuous","single-task" CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE has another value
error parsing config file, or a missing file (exit code 1) The secret is not valid YAML, or not attached with the target circleci_runner_config.yaml
circleci-runner-entrypoint: error: ... A missing prerequisite or runner: see the Linux entries

Fix. Correct the stack file or the secret and deploy again. To stop the loop meanwhile:

docker service scale runners_<SERVICE>=0

The runner log shows 401

Symptom: the log contains 401 (Unauthorized) and the runner never claims a job.

Cause. CircleCI rejected the token: it was deleted, mistyped, or belongs to another class. A drifted clock is not a 401: it fails the TLS handshake first (see the x509 entry).

Fix. Check that the secret <service>-token holds the token of the class with the same name as the service. A swapped token does not fail loudly: the runner serves the class of its token, so jobs of the intended class stay queued. On Linux the token is in the proxy: look in runners_token-proxy for upstream status 401. Then rotate the token.

The runner log shows 403 and the proxy log says refused

Symptom: the runner log has 403 (Forbidden) for the claim, and runners_token-proxy says claim from <ip> refused.

Cause. The proxy answers a claim only from an address that Swarm DNS lists now for tasks.<service> of a class it serves, once for each container. The log line gives the reason.

Fix.

  • not a runner of any class: the class is not in the proxy (a new class needs its secret and, on Linux, its network under token-proxy: Define a class), the proxy is not on the class network, or the caller is not a runner.
