  • this runner has already claimed a task: the proxy restarted while the runner was idle, moved to another node and lost its state, or latched the runner after a claim of unknown outcome (fail closed). The runner retries every 5 seconds until its idle timeout replaces it. On Linux, replace the idle runners now:

    docker service update --force --update-parallelism 0 runners_<SERVICE>

    On Windows, do not: it kills busy jobs. Remove only the refused containers (Replace refused runners on Windows). See also A claim whose outcome is unknown and Restart the proxy.

  • too many claims (429), or 503 with Retry-After: the proxy limits each client IP and serves at most 512 requests at once. A runner stays far below that, so look for a client that polls in a loop (Monitor the token proxy).

The runner log shows x509 certificate errors

Symptom: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid, or x509: certificate signed by unknown authority, and the runner never connects.

Cause. The node clock drifted, or an inspecting proxy re-signs the traffic with a CA that the container does not trust.

Fix. This must print yes. If not, fix NTP on the node.

timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value

For an inspecting proxy or your own CircleCI server CA, add the CA to your image for the runner and the jobs. The token proxy and the distributors read other stores: see Proxies and certificate authorities, component by component and Private certificate authorities.

Jobs wait while the runners are idle

Symptom: the runner inventory shows idle runners, and jobs stay queued.

Cause. The inventory shows running tasks only, and queued tasks count against concurrency. A class can sit at the maxConcurrentTasks limit of the resource class (20 by default) or at the runner concurrency of your plan. Jobs for a class with no runner queue forever and hold concurrency.

Fix. Ask the runner API how many tasks wait, and compare it with the replicas. Set RUNNER_API to the runner API of your installation (for CircleCI server).

RUNNER_API=https://runner.circleci.com
curl -s -H "Circle-Token: $CIRCLECI_API_TOKEN" "$RUNNER_API/api/v3/runner/tasks?resource-class=<NAMESPACE>/<CLASS>"

A count above 0 with idle replicas points at a limit, or at a class name that no service serves. Cancel the tasks of a class with no runners, and ask CircleCI support to raise maxConcurrentTasks (Capacity and concurrency).

Many jobs fail within seconds on one node

Symptom: jobs of a class fail within seconds or end with no work done, and docker stack ps runners lists many tasks of one node that ended seconds after they started. The node is Ready and the others are fine.

Cause. A Ready node can still fail every job it claims: a full disk, a wrong current link in the runner volume, a bad Docker engine, a clock far off, or a broken route to the registry or CircleCI. A failed task is replaced at once and claims again, so the broken node takes a large share of the jobs. Swarm does not see it, because the node answers its heartbeats.

Fix.

  1. Count the tasks that ended in the last minute for each node. A node far above the others is the one.

    docker stack ps runners --format '{{.Node}} {{.CurrentState}}' | grep -E ' (Complete|Failed) [0-9]+ seconds? ago' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
docker stack ps runners --no-trunc --format '{{.Node}} {{.Name}} {{.CurrentState}} {{.Error}}' | grep '<NODE_NAME>' | head -20

  2. Stop it from taking jobs. On Linux, drain it. On Windows, pause it instead: failing jobs free the node quickly, and a drain would kill a good job after about 5 seconds (A Windows node).

    docker node update --availability drain <NODE_NAME>

  3. Find the cause on the node (Linux):

    df -h /var/lib/docker
docker run --rm alpine true
docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine ls -l /v/current
docker ps -a --filter 'name=runners_' --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' | head
timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value

    Read the newest failed container (docker logs <container>) and journalctl -u docker -n 100. For a full disk, see Free disk space. A missing current means the distributor has not installed a runner here: The runner waits for the distributor, and then exits with code 80.

  4. Fix the cause and set the node active. If the cause is unclear, run docker swarm leave on it, then docker node rm <NODE_NAME> on a manager, and rebuild it. Rerun the failed jobs.

To see it early, alert on the count in step 1 and keep a canary job for each class.

A service update is paused or rolled back

Symptom: docker service update or docker stack deploy stops partway, and this prints paused, rollback_started or rollback_completed (the Message field names the failed task):

docker service inspect --format '{{.UpdateStatus.State}}' runners_<SERVICE>

Cause. A new task failed to start, for example exit code 80 after a wrong setting or a missing secret. The stack files set no failure_action, so Swarm pauses at the first failure, and the replicas it did not reach keep the old version.

Fix. Read why the task failed (docker service ps --no-trunc runners_<service>), correct your stack file, and deploy again with the same files. To go back at once:

docker service update --rollback runners_<SERVICE>

Refer to Update the images.

Error: The swarm does not have a leader

Symptom: a Swarm command fails with The swarm does not have a leader. It's possible that too few managers are online.

Cause. The managers lost quorum (two of three, or three of five must be online). Running jobs finish, but no replacement task starts, so capacity drops to zero.

Fix. Bring the managers back, starting with the ones stopped last, and check docker node ls on a reachable manager. If the managers are lost for good, recover from one surviving manager:

docker swarm init --force-new-cluster --advertise-addr <MANAGER_IP>

Refer to Back up the managers, and recover and Managers and quorum.

More Swarm symptoms

Symptom Cause and fix
docker stack deploy fails with secret not found: linux-default-token An external secret does not exist. Every service needs <service>-token, and on Linux every runner service also needs runner-placeholder-token. Create it, or delete the service from your copy with its entries under secrets: and networks:. On Windows, runners.yaml needs only windows-default-token, and each add-on file its own <service>-token
Swarm is encrypted and needs to be unlocked before it can be used Autolock, and this manager restarted. Run docker swarm unlock and enter the key from docker swarm unlock-key on an unlocked manager (Unlock a locked swarm)
This node is not a swarm manager You ran a Swarm command on a worker. Run it on a manager (docker node ls lists them)
docker swarm join times out or fails with a connection error The manager is not reachable on its advertised address and port 2377, or listens on loopback only. Open the Inter-node ports, and initialize the swarm with a routable --advertise-addr
Jobs queue but no runner claims them The resource_class does not equal <namespace>/<service>, the class has replicas: 0, or replicas cannot reach CircleCI. Check Runners in the web app, that the tasks run, and Egress hosts
A task is rejected with No such image or an authentication error The node cannot pull the image: registry unreachable, image private, or rate limit. Check egress, deploy with --with-registry-auth for a private registry, or use a mirror (Registry needs, What needs the internet)
docker service logs prints nothing, or less than you expect Swarm prunes old tasks of a slot with their logs (history limit 5 by default, 2 with the setup helper), and the command reads only the local, json-file and journald drivers. Use docker service ps --no-trunc, docker logs <container> on the node, and Ship the logs
A job exits with code 137, or a build fails with fork: Resource temporarily unavailable or Cannot allocate memory 137 is SIGKILL: the kernel kills a job over the memory limit (docker inspect <container> shows OOMKilled: true), or a stop outlasted stop_grace_period. More processes than limits.pids (4096) fails to fork. Raise limits.memory or limits.pids and keep the reservation equal (Size the limits)
A job fails with a message that points at an issue with your infrastructure, and its log just stops The runner stopped during the job: a node died or rebooted, a stop from outside (update, scale-down, drain) outlasted the grace period (on Windows it kills the job after about 5 seconds), or an out-of-memory kill. Find the task with docker service ps --no-trunc runners_<service>, then rerun the job: runners do not retry (Node death, Stop a busy Windows container)

Linux

The runner waits for the distributor, and then exits with code 80

Symptom: the runner log shows circleci-runner-entrypoint: waiting for the runner-distributor of this node to install the runner. After the wait (120 seconds by default) the container exits with code 80 and /opt/machine-runner-swarm/current is 'missing': the runner-distributor of this node has not installed the runner, and the loop repeats every 10 seconds.

Cause. The runner-bin volume of the node has no runner yet: the runner-distributor task of the node is not running, cannot download the runner, or refuses it. A first deploy or a node that just joined is normal: the next container starts as soon as current exists.

Fix. Check that the distributor runs on that node, and read its log:

docker service ps --no-trunc runners_runner-distributor
docker service logs --tail 50 runners_runner-distributor

A node with no task is Down, drained, or not a Linux node. Otherwise see The distributor log shows cannot download and The distributor log shows SHA-256 mismatch. To wait longer, set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_WAIT in the environment of the runner services.

Error: does not match its SHA-256 record

Symptom: the container exits with code 80 and .../versions/3.1.13/bin/circleci-runner does not match its SHA-256 record ...: refusing to start.

Cause. The binary in the volume is not the one the distributor recorded: an incomplete install, a changed volume, or a damaged disk. The entrypoint checks at every start and never runs a different binary (Runner binary integrity on Linux).

Fix. The distributor reinstalls a differing version at its next check. To do it now, force an update, which downloads the version again on every node:

docker service update --force runners_runner-distributor

If the binary changes again, find what writes to the volume: a privileged container on the node, or a person with access.

The distributor log shows cannot download

Symptom: runners_runner-distributor logs runner-distributor: cannot download <address>, for manifest.json or a tarball such as <version>/circleci-runner_linux_amd64.tar.gz. The distributor keeps its runner and retries in 5 minutes. Without a runner, the runner containers of the node end as in the entry above.

Cause. The node cannot reach circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com or your mirror (egress rule, proxy, DNS, clock), or the file is not on the mirror (for example the pinned version). An https mirror needs a certificate from a public CA, because the distributor uses the CA bundle of the stock Alpine image. A proxy rarely helps: the distributor wget reads only lowercase http_proxy, sends https:// URLs as a plain GET and not CONNECT, and ignores no_proxy.

Fix. Download the same file from the node with the same tool:

docker run --rm alpine wget -q -O /dev/null https://circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com/circleci-runner/manifest.json && echo reachable

Open the host in Egress hosts, or fix the mirror. A mirror that the node reaches without a proxy is the dependable setup (Run the downloads from a mirror, Proxies and certificate authorities, component by component).

The distributor log shows SHA-256 mismatch

Symptom: runner-distributor: SHA-256 mismatch for circleci-runner_linux_amd64.tar.gz <version>: got <hash>, wanted <hash>: refusing to install. The distributor installs nothing and retries later.

Cause. The tarball does not have the SHA-256 that the manifest, or your MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_SHA256 list, names. Usual causes: a list that lacks one architecture (a fleet with amd64 and arm64 nodes needs both), a mirror whose tarball and manifest do not match, or a proxy that changes the download.

Fix. Compare wanted with the SHA-256 of the file you expect, from the checksums.txt of the release or the manifest, and correct the list, mirror or proxy. Never copy the got value into the list without checking where the file came from.

The token-proxy service does not start: the image cannot be pulled

Symptom: docker service ps runners_token-proxy --no-trunc (Windows: runners_token-proxy-windows) shows No such image, manifest unknown, pull access denied or no matching manifest for <platform>, and runners get connection errors for token-proxy. The distributor and runner are unaffected.

Cause. The image is ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy, or what MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE names. Usual causes: the node cannot reach Docker Hub, the tag does not exist (a typo, or edge before the first publication of the main branch), a local image such as machine-runner-swarm-proxy:dev that exists on another node, or a platform the tag lacks (Windows on Arm).

Fix. Check the name and pull it on the node:

docker service inspect runners_token-proxy --format '{{.Spec.TaskTemplate.ContainerSpec.Image}}'
docker pull <IMAGE>

Behind an allow list, add Docker Hub (Egress hosts), or mirror the image and set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE (Upgrade the token proxy). A local build must be on the node that runs the proxy: build it there, or docker save <IMAGE> | ssh <NODE> docker load. Swarm retries by itself.

Error: must be owned by root and not group/world writable

Symptom: the container exits with code 80 and .../versions/3.1.13/bin/circleci-runner must be owned by root and not group/world writable.

Cause. The entrypoint refuses a runner that the job user or runner user can replace. The distributor makes the volume files root-owned with mode 0755, so something changed them.

Fix. Set the owner and mode again on the node:

docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v alpine sh -c 'chown -R 0:0 /v && chmod -R go-w /v'

Error: failed to remove working directory, permission denied

Symptom: every task fails, with failed to remove working directory before starting task or ... while cleaning up task (or could not clean up task), each with permission denied.

Cause. Someone set CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR to true on a Linux service. The runner (uid 2000) removes its working directory itself, but the job user owns that directory and its files, so even the first task fails. The stack files and the entrypoint default it to false for this reason.

Fix. Set CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR: "false", or remove the variable so the default applies, and deploy again. A single-task container is discarded after the job, so nothing is lost. In a persistent class, start every job with a step that removes what an earlier job left (Working directory cleanup).

Permission denied on /opt/machine-runner-swarm with SELinux

Symptom: on RHEL, a replica reports Permission denied for files under /opt/machine-runner-swarm while SELinux is enforcing.

Cause. Untested here: CI does not run on RHEL. Docker normally labels volume files for containers. When it does not, the files keep a type that containers may not read, and a Swarm service mount has no :z option to relabel them.

Fix. Confirm the denial, then label the volume on the node. Files the distributor writes later inherit the label.

sudo ausearch -m avc -ts recent
sudo chcon -R -t container_file_t /var/lib/docker/volumes/runners_runner-bin/_data

Keep SELinux enforcing. If you needed this, open an issue with the avc line.

More Linux symptoms

Symptom Cause and fix
Exit code 80 with jobs cannot be stepped down in this image: it needs sudo or util-linux setpriv The image has neither sudo nor util-linux setpriv, or no setpriv and no su to start the runner. A hardened class (MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO=false) needs util-linux setpriv even if the image has sudo. Add the packages in a derived image (What an image needs)
The distributor logs current is <version> (major <n>), not 3: not adopting it, or current has SHA-256 <hash>, which no versioned release of the manifest has: not adopting it The first: current moved to another major version, and the distributor keeps its version. Read the runner changelog, try it, then set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_MAJOR or pin the version (Pin a version). The second: the mirror has an old or edited manifest.json. Copy it again, with the tarball of the version current names
Every sudo in a job prints unable to send audit message The AUDIT_WRITE capability is dropped. Keep it out of cap_drop (a hardened class keeps it in cap_add)
In the hardened class, apt-get install fails with Permission denied, or sudo says the user may not run sudo By design: the class steps jobs down with setpriv --no-new-privs. Build the tools into the image (Bring your own image)
docker build fails with Cannot connect to the Docker daemon By design: the class mounts no Docker engine. Use the opt-in class or a daemonless builder (Docker Builds)
A docker-build job fails with permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket The entrypoint adds the job user to the socket’s group but skips group id 0, so a root:root socket gives no access. Give the host socket a group that is not root, normally docker (SocketGroup=docker in the systemd socket unit), check that stat -c '%U:%G %g' /var/run/docker.sock shows a group id above 0, and deploy again
no space left on device, Docker commands fail, or the node stops taking jobs Each finished job leaves a stopped container (Swarm keeps five tasks per slot by default), plus images, build cache and logs. Stop the node from taking jobs, free the space and set the history limit (Free disk space). It can look like Many jobs fail within seconds on one node

Windows

Symptom Cause and fix
Task rejected with 0xc0370101: The container operating system does not match the host operating system The image build is newer than the host. A Server 2022 host runs only ltsc2022 images, a Server 2025 host ltsc2025 and ltsc2022. Labels normally prevent this, so look for a node with a label it should not have. Use a tag the host can run, and set the machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022 and windows-ltsc2025 labels to match (Image tags and host builds)
The container runs but the runner never claims a job and logs no clear error Without SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege the runner retries the task agent download forever. This happens when the container runs as a user other than ContainerAdministrator. Never set user: in a Windows service or change USER in a derived image
Log says circleci-runner <version> is in use: removing it at a later check Windows cannot remove files that a running container uses. Nothing to do: the distributor removes the version at a later check
docker swarm init fails with could not find the system's IP address - specify one with --advertise-addr Pass the host IPv4 address: docker swarm init --advertise-addr <HOST_IPV4> (also on a host with several adapters, and Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm requires -AdvertiseAddr)
Downloads fail with Unable to connect to the remote server or no such host for a few seconds after docker swarm init Pull the images first and run docker swarm init last. The distributor retries its downloads
Overlay network creation fails on a host with one adapter An existing transparent network can block overlay networks. Move it to a second adapter or remove it (Microsoft documentation on Windows container networking)
The first task on a host takes a long time The node pulls the Server Core image (about 2.2 GB compressed) when the first task lands. Run docker pull for the image on each node before you deploy
Setup.ps1 reports CHECK windows-server FAIL The helper supports Windows Server 2022 (build 20348) and 2025 (build 26100). Server 2019 is untested and has no label in the stack files, so it needs your own image tag, label and constraint
persist_to_workspace or attach_workspace reports a missing tar or gzip The Git mount is missing, or the service PATH lacks C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin (a service PATH replaces the image one). Keep both mounts and the full PATH from the shipped file
C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\tar.exe fails with Cannot stat when you run it by hand with a backslash path The task agent runs this tar.exe from the drive root with --force-local and forward-slash operands relative to the root (for C:\cci\w\ws it passes cci/w/ws). Use the same form in your test
hcs::System::Start: context deadline exceeded An image build used New-Item -Force on an existing registry key, which deletes its values and subkeys. On HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\cexecsvc that removes the container exec service. Rebuild the image and set values with reg add or Set-ItemProperty

The runner never starts: cannot access path current

Symptom: docker service ps --no-trunc runners_windows-default shows tasks failing with cannot access path ...\runner-bin\_data\current (or ...\git\current) or invalid mount config, and Swarm starts the next task after 10 seconds.

Cause. runner-distributor-windows has not flipped the links current and git\current of the volume on this node yet. This is normal on a new node (the first download of the runner and portable Git takes a few minutes). It lasts when the distributor cannot install.

Fix. Read its log:

docker service logs runners_runner-distributor-windows

A SHA-256 mismatch, cannot download or not adopting it line names the cause. The service must have a task on the node (docker service ps runners_runner-distributor-windows), so the node needs the label machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022=true and the base image pulled. Behind a proxy, set HTTPS_PROXY on the distributor service (it reads only HTTPS_PROXY, no NO_PROXY). Without internet access, refer to Upgrade the runner on Windows.

Container exits with code 3221225786 after a stop

Symptom: a job ends about 5 seconds after a rolling update, scale-down, node drain or docker stop, and docker service ps --no-trunc shows task: non-zero exit (3221225786) (0xC000013A).

Cause. The container was stopped from outside while it ran a job, and Windows gives a stock Server Core container about 5 seconds, whatever stop_grace_period says. A job that finishes by itself does not end this way.

Fix. Rerun the interrupted jobs, and change a service only while its class runs no job (Stop a busy Windows container).

Collect information for a bug report

Gather the output of these commands, remove tokens, and open an issue.

docker version
docker node ls
docker stack ps runners --no-trunc
docker service logs --tail 200 runners_<SERVICE>
docker service logs --tail 200 runners_token-proxy

On Linux, add the runner version (run on the node) and the distributor log:

docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine cat /v/current/VERSION
docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor

On Windows, add the distributor log:

docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor-windows

item.title: Install on Windows Server with Docker Swarm
item.description:
This page deploys CircleCI machine runner 3 as a Docker Swarm stack on Windows Server. Every job runs in a new Windows Server Core container, and Swarm replaces the container after the job. The steps cover one host (Multi-Node Clusters adds more). For a first run, Quickstart on Windows Server is shorter.

Note

If you can run Kubernetes, CircleCI recommends container runner for containerized jobs. This page is for teams that run Docker Swarm and need a clean Windows container for every job.

Status. This is a CircleCI Labs project, 0.x, and CircleCI support does not cover it. It is tested against CircleCI cloud only: What is tested says how. Replicas are fixed: the stack does not add or remove nodes, and it does not scale to the queue.

The steps: start or join a swarm, label the node, create the secrets, deploy. The optional setup helper runs most of them.

Important

The services run the stock Server Core image, and no image is built. Stopping a busy container from outside kills its job after about 5 seconds, so change a Windows class while it is idle (Stop a busy Windows container).

Prerequisites

  • A CircleCI cloud organization and a user who is an organization admin. CircleCI server is not tested: CircleCI server says what is known.
  • The CircleCI CLI 1.4.0 or later, signed in. It can run on your workstation. Pass --org <org> (a slug such as gh/my-org, or a UUID): without it the CLI uses the organization of the git remote of the current directory, which in a clone of this repository is not yours.
  • One or more Windows Server hosts (table below). The host cannot be a domain controller.
  • Docker Engine 28.0 or later (CLI and engine), in Windows-container mode, with the Windows Containers feature (enabling it restarts the host). The stack files mount a subpath of a volume (current and git\current), which older CLIs and engines ignore: the runner would not start. CI runs Docker 29.4.0 on Windows, and windows\Setup.ps1 checks the version. The Install-DockerCE script in the helpful_tools directory of the Microsoft Windows Containers repository installs both.
  • An elevated Windows PowerShell 5.1 session.
  • A host clock synchronized with NTP. TLS to CircleCI fails silently when the clock drifts.
  • Outbound HTTPS from each host to the hosts in Egress hosts: circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com (the runner and its manifest), github.com and release-assets.githubusercontent.com (Git and 7-Zip), mcr.microsoft.com (the base image), and Docker Hub (the token proxy image). What needs internet lists everything. Not tested without internet access: Upgrade the runner on Windows.
  • Disk: servercore is about 2.2 GB compressed. Each container shows 20 GB free on C: by default. To raise the limit, add "storage-opts": ["size=60GB"] to C:\ProgramData\docker\config\daemon.json. Every finished container keeps its layer until Swarm prunes it.
  • CPU and memory for the services, and runner concurrency in your CircleCI plan for your replicas (Size the limits).
Windows Server Machine runner 3 Status in this repository
2025 Compatible Tested in CI, image tag ltsc2025
2022 Compatible Tested in CI, image tag ltsc2022
2019 Compatible Untested here: the stack files have no label or placement for it
2016 and older Not compatible Not supported

Image tags and host builds

With process isolation, the image build must be the host build or an older one. Label every node with the image tags it can run: a service is placed on a node that carries the label of its image tag.

Host Images it can run Node labels
Windows Server 2022 ltsc2022 only machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022=true
Windows Server 2025 ltsc2025 and ltsc2022 machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022=true and machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2025=true

The shipped services use ltsc2022 images, so they run on 2022 and 2025 nodes. A service on an ltsc2025 image requires machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2025 == true, so it runs on 2025 nodes only. A mismatch that the labels do not catch fails with 0xc0370101.

Self-hosted runner terms agreement

An organization admin must agree to the CircleCI Runner Terms before you install self-hosted runners through the web app. Through the CLI, you agree by installing and using them (details). Whether the token proxy between your runners and CircleCI is covered is for your own review: this project does not give legal advice.

Get the files

Use a release (recommended) or clone the repository at a release tag. Paths on this page are relative to the root of either. The GitHub release has the bundle machine-runner-swarm-<version>.zip, and the Linux page lists every file of a release.

git clone --branch <release-tag> https://github.com/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm.git
cd machine-runner-swarm

Install cosign

cosign 3.1.3 or a later 3.x verifies the release (CI signs and verifies with 3.1.3, and earlier versions are not tested). Download the executable and the checksum list of the cosign release, compare the checksum, and put the file in a directory on your PATH:

$cosign = '3.1.3'
$u = "https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v$cosign"
Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "$u/cosign-windows-amd64.exe" -OutFile cosign.exe
Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "$u/cosign_checksums.txt" -OutFile cosign_checksums.txt
$want = ((Get-Content cosign_checksums.txt | Where-Object { $_ -match '\scosign-windows-amd64\.exe$' }) -split '\s+')[0]
if ((Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath cosign.exe).Hash.ToLower() -ne $want) { throw 'the checksum of cosign.exe does not match: stop' }
.\cosign.exe version

This checks the file against a list from the same place: it catches a damaged download, not a compromised release page. Your own package manager is another source.

Verify a release

CircleCI signs the file SHA256SUMS of each release with the OIDC token of the job that makes the release. The signature proves that a job of this CircleCI project made the file, and the checksum proves that your download is the file that the job made. The Linux page explains what the signature proves, and what it does not.

Set $version once to the number of the latest release without the v, and read its notes. The download fails while the placeholder is unchanged.

$version = 'X.Y.Z'
$base = "https://github.com/CircleCI-Labs/machine-runner-swarm/releases/download/v$version"
$zip = "machine-runner-swarm-$version.zip"

Then paste this block. It stops at the first failing check. The variables are set outside it, because & runs the block in a scope of its own. Only a bundle that passes the signature, the ref and the checksum is unpacked.

& {
 $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
 foreach ($f in $zip, 'SHA256SUMS', 'SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json') { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri "$base/$f" -OutFile $f }

 # 1. the signature: the CircleCI project and pipeline definition of this repository signed SHA256SUMS
 cosign verify-blob SHA256SUMS --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json `
 --certificate-identity 'https://circleci.com/api/v2/projects/7bbdbb66-6ba8-4f6c-982e-d4fb401ec257/pipeline-definitions/8b2a66db-3f28-5c80-88e4-03f4694b5b60' `
 --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://oidc.circleci.com'
 if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'the signature does not verify: stop' }

 # 2. the ref: a job of any branch can sign with that identity, so the certificate must also say that the job ran for refs/heads/main
 # (the long string is the OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.14 followed by the value refs/heads/main)
 $material = (Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json | ConvertFrom-Json).verificationMaterial
 if ($material.certificate) { $cert = $material.certificate.rawBytes } else { $cert = $material.x509CertificateChain.certificates[0].rawBytes }
 $hex = -join ([Convert]::FromBase64String($cert) | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString('x2') })
 if ($hex -notmatch '^([0-9a-f]{2})*2b0601040183bf30010e0411(0c|13)0f726566732f68656164732f6d61696e') { throw 'NOT signed for refs/heads/main: stop' }

 # 3. the file: its checksum is in the signed list
 $want = ((Get-Content SHA256SUMS | Where-Object { $_ -match "\s$([regex]::Escape($zip))$" }) -split '\s+')[0]
 if ((Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath $zip).Hash.ToLower() -ne $want) { throw "the checksum of $zip is not the signed one: stop" }

 # only a verified bundle is unpacked
 Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $zip -DestinationPath .
 'RELEASE VERIFIED'
}

Continue only when the last line is RELEASE VERIFIED. Anything else, an error message or no output at all, means that the release is not verified: delete the downloaded files, and start again or ask in an issue. The ref check exists because the signing identity is the same for every branch, so the block reads the certificate extension 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.14 (the OID in the long string) and fails unless its value is refs/heads/main. The pattern starts on a byte boundary, and ASN.1 tag 0c or 13 is the string type of the value.

Then change into the bundle:

cd "machine-runner-swarm-$version"

The token proxy image has its own signature: Verify the token proxy image has the commands.

The token proxy image

The token proxy holds your class tokens (The token proxy). On Windows it is the image ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy of Docker Hub (ccilabs is the Docker Hub organization of CircleCI Labs), which the stack file token-proxy-windows pulls on deploy: a static binary on Nano Server, for windows/amd64. The name is not the trust root: the signature check is. One tag also holds the Linux images, and a manifest list holds one Windows image for Server 2022 and one for Server 2025, so Docker picks the one of the host. Tags, pinning and the signature are the same as on Linux: The token proxy image and Verify the token proxy image.

The image runs as ContainerAdministrator, as the stock Server Core image does, because ContainerUser of Nano Server cannot write to the volume that keeps the state of the proxy.

There is no windows/arm64 image, because CI has no Windows on Arm host to build and test one on. In a cluster with Windows on Arm nodes, pin the proxy to a windows/amd64 node with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_PLACEMENT (Multi-Node Clusters). A cluster of only Windows on Arm nodes needs an image of your own: build the proxy with GOARCH=arm64, build proxy\Dockerfile.windows on an arm64 host with an arm64 Nano Server image as --build-arg BASE=, and name it with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE.

To use another image (development, an air gap), set MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE in the environment of docker stack deploy. The image must be on the node that runs the proxy: a local build exists only where you built it. This builds one from a checkout: build the binary on any host with Go, then build the image on the Windows host whose build matches the base image.

$env:GOOS = 'windows'; $env:GOARCH = 'amd64'; $env:CGO_ENABLED = '0'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path build | Out-Null
Push-Location proxy; go build -trimpath -o ..\build\machine-runner-swarm-proxy.exe .\cmd\machine-runner-swarm-proxy; Pop-Location
docker build -f proxy\Dockerfile.windows -t machine-runner-swarm-proxy:dev build
$env:MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_IMAGE = 'machine-runner-swarm-proxy:dev'

1. Create the resource classes

  1. Create a namespace if your organization has none.

    circleci namespace create <namespace> --org <org>

  2. Create one resource class for each service in the stack files. The class name must equal the service name. The shipped windows\stack\runners.yaml has the service windows-default and deploys on its own.

    circleci runner resource-class create <namespace>/windows-default --org <org> --generate-token

The command prints the token once: store it in your secret manager. The optional add-on files in the same directory add windows-custom (custom-image.yaml), windows-persistent (persistent.yaml), windows-docker-build (docker-build.yaml) and windows-default-ssh (ssh-rerun.yaml, untested). Create the classes you plan to use.

2. Prepare each host

Run these steps in an elevated PowerShell on every host, before you start Swarm: the network of the host drops for a few seconds after docker swarm init, and the pull needs it.

  1. Confirm that Docker runs Windows containers. The command prints windows.

    docker info --format '{{.OSType}}'

  2. Pull the base image of the shipped services once, so the first task does not wait for it. A Server 2025 host runs ltsc2022 images too, so this is the image for both hosts. Pull ltsc2025 as well only for a service that you put on that image.

    docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022

  3. On the host that runs the token proxy (a manager, by default), pull its image too, or build your own (The token proxy image).

    docker pull ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy:latest

3. Start Swarm and label the node

  1. On the first host, start Swarm. Always pass --advertise-addr with the IPv4 address of the host: a plain docker swarm init fails on some hosts with could not find the system's IP address. For more than one node, see Multi-Node Clusters.

    docker swarm init --advertise-addr <host IPv4 address>

  2. Label the node with the image tags it can run. A Server 2022 node gets the first label, and a Server 2025 node gets both.

    docker node update --label-add machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022=true <node name>
docker node update --label-add machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2025=true <node name>

On a single node, the token proxy needs no label: it runs on the manager, and the jobs run there too. In a cluster, give the proxy a node of its own: label it machine-runner-swarm.proxy=true, and runner services never run there, so a job never shares a node with the proxy. Do not set the label on the only node of a swarm, because no runner would be placed. If the managers are Linux hosts, or there are several managers, also pin the proxy to a Windows node with the placement in the environment of docker stack deploy:

docker node update --label-add machine-runner-swarm.proxy=true <node name>
$env:MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_PROXY_PLACEMENT = 'node.labels.machine-runner-swarm.proxy == true'

Without a matching node the proxy stays pending and no runner can claim (Where the proxy runs, and when it moves). The optional classes need one more label each, on the nodes that run them:

Class Label
windows-docker-build machine-runner-swarm.docker-build=true
windows-persistent machine-runner-swarm.class.windows-persistent=true

4. Create the secrets

Create one secret for each service you deploy, named <service>-token, including each optional class (windows-persistent-token too: persistent.yaml declares it as external, so the deploy fails without it). It is a runner config file that holds only the token:

api:
 auth_token: <token>

The token proxy mounts the secrets of the proxied classes, and those runners never see them. The persistent class is the exception (The persistent class). The runners read one more secret, runner-placeholder-token, with a made-up token in the same format (the setup helper creates it). Swarm mounts it at C:\ProgramData\Docker\secrets\circleci_runner_config.yaml, and the runner reads it with --config. Every other runner setting is a CIRCLECI_RUNNER_* variable in the stack file.

This block asks for the token with hidden input and passes the config to docker secret create on stdin, so no file with the token is written on the host. Repeat the first part for each class, with its name in $class. Create the placeholder once.

$class = 'windows-default'
$secure = Read-Host -Prompt "Runner token for $class" -AsSecureString
$bstr = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::SecureStringToBSTR($secure)
try { $token = [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::PtrToStringBSTR($bstr) } finally { [Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::ZeroFreeBSTR($bstr) }
if (-not $token) { throw "no token entered for $class" }
"api:`n auth_token: $token`n" | docker secret create "$class-token" -
Remove-Variable token
"api:`n auth_token: machine-runner-swarm-placeholder`n" | docker secret create runner-placeholder-token -

Windows does not support the uid, gid and mode options of secrets: only administrators and SYSTEM can read the file inside the container, and jobs run as an administrator. Swarm also writes the secret in clear text to the disk of the container until it stops, which is a Swarm limitation on Windows (Linux keeps it in memory). Enable BitLocker on the Docker volume (Token model on each OS).

5. Review the stack files

Copy windows\stack to a directory of your own, deploy\, and keep it under version control. From here on you check and deploy your copies and never the files under windows\stack. For a first run, change nothing.

Copy-Item -Recurse windows\stack deploy

Check that the file parses. This needs no running Swarm.

docker stack config -c deploy\runners.yaml | Out-Null

The directory holds the stack files and runner-distributor.ps1, the script that runners.yaml ships as a Swarm config (file: runner-distributor.ps1): keep it next to runners.yaml. Review these first (Resource Classes has the details):

Service File Purpose
runner-distributor-windows runners.yaml Installs and upgrades the runner and Git on every Windows node. Keep it in your copy
windows-default runners.yaml Stock Server Core image, two replicas
windows-custom custom-image.yaml Your own image on top of stock Server Core (Images). It has a placeholder image that you replace
windows-persistent persistent.yaml A long-lived runner with a named volume (Persistent mode)
windows-docker-build docker-build.yaml Builds Windows images with the host engine (Docker Builds)
windows-default-ssh ssh-rerun.yaml Rerun job with SSH, port 54782. Untested on Windows (Rerun job with SSH)
  • runners.yaml needs the secrets windows-default-token and runner-placeholder-token. Each add-on file needs its own <service>-token.
  • The distributor settings (the runner version, a mirror, an explicit SHA-256 list) are variables of docker stack deploy and need no edit (Upgrade the runner on Windows).
  • For a class on the ltsc2025 image, copy a service under a new name and resource class, use the ltsc2025 image tag, and set the constraint node.labels.machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2025 == true.
  • Add each optional file with another -c flag, and pass the same list on every deploy (how the files merge). Each add-on file repeats the anchors of runners.yaml and declares the volume runner-bin, so it also loads alone: change a common setting in every file you use.

To check the optional files, pass them all in the order you deploy them:

docker stack config -c deploy\runners.yaml -c deploy\custom-image.yaml -c deploy\persistent.yaml -c deploy\docker-build.yaml | Out-Null

For the keys that Windows honours and ignores, see Stack keys on Windows.

6. Deploy the stack

Deploy your copy from step 5:

docker stack deploy -c deploy\runners.yaml runners

To add optional classes, pass your copies after runners.yaml with more -c flags, for example your own image on top of stock Server Core:

docker stack deploy -c deploy\runners.yaml -c deploy\custom-image.yaml runners

This is the whole install: nothing is staged on the host. The service runner-distributor-windows starts on every Windows node, downloads the pinned runner version (the newest that CI tests) and the pinned portable Git (about 60 MB, 406 MB unpacked), verifies their SHA-256 checksums (the runner against the values the stack file carries, not CircleCI’s manifest), installs them into the per-node volume runner-bin, and flips two links. The runner services mount the volume read-only twice: current at C:\machine-runner-swarm, and git\current at C:\Program Files\Git, where the task agent expects tar.exe. The stock Server Core image needs no changes, and circleci-runner.exe is the main process of the container.

On a new node the first runner tasks fail with cannot access path ... \current until the distributor has flipped the link, which takes a few minutes for the first download. Swarm starts the next task after the restart delay of 10 seconds, so nothing needs to be done. Watch the distributor:

docker service logs runners_runner-distributor-windows

Verify the deployment

  1. List the services and tasks. The service runners_runner-distributor-windows shows one replica for each Windows node.

    docker stack services runners
docker stack ps runners --no-trunc

  2. Check that the runners connected. Each replica is listed as online, named <node hostname>-<service>-<slot>. The web app shows the same under Runners.

    circleci runner instance list --org <org> --resource-class <namespace>/windows-default

  3. Run a job. The quickstart has a complete config, and examples/windows-job.yml has more steps. Run the workflow twice: the two runs print different values for $MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_INSTANCE_ID, because each job runs in a new container.

What jobs can use

  • The default shell is Git Bash (bash -eo pipefail). Set shell: powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass for Windows PowerShell 5.1, or shell: cmd.exe, per job or step.
  • The working directory is C:\cci\w, and the task agent lives in C:\cci\agent. The PATH of the service reaches every step.
  • checkout, caches, test results and artifacts need Git and outbound access. Workspaces use the tar and gzip from the mounted Git.
  • OpenID Connect tokens need a writable %TEMP%.
  • The stack enables Git long paths through the environment. The registry value LongPathsEnabled is not set: a job that needs long paths for other tools sets it itself, or in its own image.
  • Not supported: desktop or UI automation, Docker commands in jobs (except the opt-in docker-build class), and service containers.
  • Not tested: add_ssh_keys, Hyper-V isolation, group managed service accounts, and proxies.
  • MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO and MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_USER of the Linux entrypoint do not exist on Windows, and Windows ignores them. There is no step-down.

Optional: use the setup helper

windows\Setup.ps1 checks the host, starts Swarm on request, labels the node, creates the secrets, and deploys. It does not install the runner: the distributor service of the stack does that on every node. It runs in an elevated Windows PowerShell 5.1 session and is safe to run again. It prints CHECK <name> PASS or FAIL for each preflight check (administrator, Windows Server build, Windows-container mode, Docker 28.0 or later, Swarm manager), and ends with Next: and the steps still to do, or Check: and the commands that watch the start.

Parameter Effect
-InitSwarm -AdvertiseAddr <ip> Creates a Swarm when none exists, and waits until the node is a manager. The address is needed only then: on an active Swarm, -InitSwarm changes nothing
-Class <name>,<name> Asks for each token with hidden input and creates the secret <name>-token. An existing secret stays unchanged
(placeholder) With -Class or -Deploy, it also creates the secret runner-placeholder-token with a made-up token, which every runner reads
-Deploy Runs docker stack deploy with -StackFile (one or more files, runners.yaml first) and -StackName (default runners). Without -StackFile it deploys the shipped windows\stack\runners.yaml as it is, which suits a first run. Once you keep copies as in step 5, pass them. It prints the files it deploys

The helper labels the node from the host build: windows-ltsc2022=true on Server 2022, and both windows-ltsc2022=true and windows-ltsc2025=true on Server 2025 (machine-runner-swarm. prefix). It supports Server 2022 and 2025 only, and does not add the labels of the optional classes. The distributor reads its settings from the environment of -Deploy.

The first command is a first run with the shipped runners.yaml. The second deploys your copy from step 5, with its optional file.

.\windows\Setup.ps1 -InitSwarm -AdvertiseAddr 10.0.0.5 -Class windows-default -Deploy
.\windows\Setup.ps1 -Class windows-default,windows-custom -StackFile .\deploy\runners.yaml,.\deploy\custom-image.yaml -Deploy

Upgrade

The distributor pins the exact runner version that this release tests, with the SHA-256 values of its tarballs, and the nodes keep it until you change it. 3.1, 3 or current (weaker: they trust the hash of the manifest) follow CircleCI’s manifest and check every 24 hours. A pin of your own is two variables of docker stack deploy: the version and its SHA-256 values (or manifest for an exact version without a list). Running jobs keep their version, and the runner services never restart (Upgrade the runner on Windows).

A new release of this repository changes the shipped stack files, and your copy deploy\ is not updated by itself. To merge, with git from Git for Windows or another diff and merge tool:

  1. Read the notes of the release and the changelog: entries marked [BREAKING] say what to change. This is a 0.x project, so a minor release can change the files.

  2. Verify and unpack the new release beside the old one (Verify a release). The old directory is the base of the merge.

  3. See what changed between the two releases, and merge each file that differs into your copy. git merge-file edits the file in place, marks conflicts with <<<<<<< lines, and exits with the number of conflicts.

    git diff --no-index "machine-runner-swarm-$old\windows\stack" "machine-runner-swarm-$new\windows\stack"
git merge-file deploy\runners.yaml "machine-runner-swarm-$old\windows\stack\runners.yaml" "machine-runner-swarm-$new\windows\stack\runners.yaml"

    Repeat for the other files you copied. Take runner-distributor.ps1 of the new release unless you edited it (Upgrade to a new release of this repository explains the names of the Swarm configs).

  4. Check deploy.replicas, image, deploy.placement.constraints and deploy.resources, the runner version pin with its SHA-256 values (a release changes them together), and the token proxy image (a release names it by digest).

  5. Check the result.

    docker stack config -c deploy\runners.yaml | Out-Null

  6. Deploy while the classes are idle (Stop a busy Windows container), with the same list of -c files as before.

    docker stack deploy -c deploy\runners.yaml runners

To roll back, deploy the previous copy.

Stop and uninstall

Refer to Uninstall. Every stop of a busy service kills its job after about 5 seconds. Refer to Stop a busy Windows container.

Troubleshooting

Refer to Troubleshooting. The most common problems are an image tag that does not match the host build, a distributor that has not installed the runner yet, and a job that ends about 5 seconds after a stop. A task also stays pending when no node carries the machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022 label (or windows-ltsc2025, for a service on an ltsc2025 image).

Additional resources

  • Concepts
  • Resource Classes
  • Security
  • Operations
  • Machine runner 3 on Windows

item.title: Concepts
item.description:
The stack runs CircleCI machine runner 3 as Docker Swarm services. Swarm handles replicas, restarts, secrets, and placement. This repository adds a stack file for each operating system, a small entrypoint and a runner distributor service for Linux, and optional setup helpers. Read this page before you change a stack file or choose between the default and the hardened class.

Services are resource classes

Each Swarm service is one CircleCI resource class. The service name is the short name of the class, so the service linux-default serves the resource class <namespace>/linux-default. A job selects the class in its config:

jobs:
 build:
 machine: true
 resource_class: <namespace>/linux-default

Each service also has one Swarm secret, <service>-token, which holds the token of that class. In the single-task classes the token proxy holds it, and the runners hold a made-up placeholder. A persistent class mounts its token in the runner container itself.

flowchart TB
nodes["Nodes: Linux amd64, Linux arm64, Windows<br/>Labels decide where tasks may run"]
subgraph services["Swarm services: one for each resource class"]
direction LR
s1["linux-default<br/>replicas: 2"]
s2["linux-python<br/>replicas: 1"]
s3["windows-default<br/>replicas: 2"]
end
r1["container 1"]
r2["container 2"]
r3["container 1"]
r4["container 1"]
r5["container 2"]
api["runner.circleci.com<br/>Runners connect outbound over HTTPS 443 only"]
nodes --> services
s1 --> r1 & r2
s2 --> r3
s3 --> r4 & r5
r1 & r2 & r3 & r4 & r5 --> api

The runner containers poll CircleCI for work. Nothing connects to a runner, so the stack publishes no ports.

deploy.replicas is the number of runners in the class, and so the number of jobs it runs at the same time. A replica that fits on no node stays Pending until capacity is free. Resource Classes covers sizing.

The token proxy

The service token-proxy of runners.yaml (on Windows token-proxy-windows, which works the same way, with the differences in Windows) keeps the class tokens away from the runners and their jobs. A runner sends its API calls to the proxy (CIRCLECI_RUNNER_API_URL: http://token-proxy:8080) and holds only a placeholder token. The proxy adds the class token to one call, the task claim, and passes every other call on to CircleCI. The runner and its task agent use the task token from the claim response for the rest.

flowchart LR
subgraph cls["Class overlay networks"]
r1["linux-default runners<br/>placeholder token"]
r2["linux-python runners<br/>placeholder token"]
end
p["token-proxy<br/>one replica<br/>holds every class token"]
api["runner.circleci.com"]
r1 -- "claim, task calls" --> p
r2 -- "claim, task calls" --> p
p -- "HTTPS: the class token on the claim only" --> api

The network decides who may claim, not what a runner says. The proxy allows a claim only from an address that Swarm DNS lists now for tasks.<service> of a class, once for each container. A container that is not a runner, or a runner that claims a second time, gets 403. A claim whose outcome is unknown counts as a claim, so the proxy fails closed. The token proxy lists what it protects and what it does not, and Monitor the token proxy covers what happens when it is down.

What it changes for you:

  • Secrets. You create the class secrets <service>-token, and one more, runner-placeholder-token, with a made-up token. Only the proxy mounts the class secrets. Every runner mounts the placeholder.
  • Classes. A new single-task class needs two lines in the proxy: its network (Linux) and its secret <service>-token. See Resource classes. The persistent classes do not use the proxy.
  • The image. ccilabs/machine-runner-swarm-proxy on Docker Hub (the signature is the trust root, not the name): a static Go binary on a minimal base, with no shell. One tag covers Linux amd64, arm64, ppc64le and s390x, and Windows Server 2022 and 2025 (amd64). Swarm pulls it, and every digest is signed: The token proxy image, Verify the token proxy image.
  • The state. The proxy keeps the addresses of the runners that have claimed in the volume proxy-state, on the node that it runs on (a manager by default). If it moves, the state stays behind: Where the proxy runs, and when it moves. In a cluster, label the node machine-runner-swarm.proxy=true: runner services never run on a node with that label, so jobs do not share a node with the proxy. On a single node, set no label.

Add-on stack files and how they merge

Each operating system has one main stack file, runners.yaml, that defines the default classes and deploys on its own. Optional classes live in add-on stack files next to it:

File System Adds
persistent.yaml, docker-build.yaml, ssh-rerun.yaml Linux and Windows Persistent, Docker-build and SSH-rerun classes
custom-image.yaml Windows A class with your own image
microvm.yaml Linux MicroVM classes (MicroVM jobs)
container-mode.yaml Linux The prototype container agent for Docker-executor jobs (Container mode)

An add-on stack file is not a patch of the main file. It defines services of its own, and each service needs its own resource class and <service>-token secret. On Linux, docker-build.yaml, ssh-rerun.yaml, and microvm.yaml also add their classes to the token-proxy service, so deploy them together with runners.yaml. persistent.yaml and container-mode.yaml keep their own tokens and do not touch the proxy.

docker stack deploy -c runners.yaml -c persistent.yaml runners merges the files in the order given, as Docker Compose does for several -f files. A service, network, secret, or volume that only one file defines is added, and a key that several files set takes the value of the later file. YAML anchors work inside one file only, so each add-on stack file repeats the common service settings.

Pass the same files, in the same order, on every deploy: the services of a file you leave out stay as they are and stop following your edits, and --prune removes them. Check a merge without a Swarm with docker stack config -c runners.yaml -c persistent.yaml.

Single-task and continuous mode

The stack files set the runner mode with CIRCLECI_RUNNER_MODE.

Mode Value Behavior Environment
Single-task single-task (default in every stack file) The runner claims one job, runs it, and exits. Swarm starts a new container for the next job Clean for every job
Continuous continuous (persistent classes only) The runner stays up and claims job after job in the same container Shared by all jobs on that runner

Use continuous mode only for trusted projects that need warm caches: Persistent mode.

Job lifecycle

Swarm never reuses a container. Every exit (a finished job, an idle timeout, a crash) leads to a new task and a new container, because the restart policy is condition: any.

sequenceDiagram
participant S as Swarm
participant C as Container
participant A as runner.circleci.com
participant N as New container
S->>C: start a task from the image
C->>A: poll for a job (single-task mode)
A-->>C: claim one job
C->>C: run the job in a clean container
C-->>S: runner exits, container stops
Note over S: restart_policy any, delay 10s
S->>N: create a NEW task and container
N->>A: poll for the next job

On Linux the entrypoint checks the runner, sets up the users, and starts it, and the runner steps the job down to the job user. On Windows the runner is the main process. Timing:

  • A replica needs about 10 seconds (the restart delay) plus container start-up before it can claim the next job. The other replicas keep claiming in the meantime.
  • Every new container downloads the task agent from circleci-binary-releases.s3.amazonaws.com. Allow this host in your egress rules.
  • A single-task runner that finds no job exits after CIRCLECI_RUNNER_IDLE_TIMEOUT (1h in the stack files), so idle replicas pick up a rotated secret or a new image within an hour.

Stopping a service sends SIGTERM to the runner. The runner drains: it accepts no new job and lets the running job finish. The stack sets stop_grace_period: 5h5m, the runner max_run_time of 5 hours plus 5 minutes.

On Windows, stop_grace_period does not hold a busy container: a stop from outside kills its job after about 5 seconds. An update, a scale-down, or a node drain is affected, so change a Windows service while its class is idle (Stop a busy Windows container).

What a clean environment covers

A clean environment means that a job starts in a container created from the image, with nothing left by an earlier job.

Covered Not covered
Files and installed packages anywhere in the container filesystem Anything on a mounted volume: persistent classes keep a named volume by design
The home directory, /tmp, and the working directory The Docker engine of the node when a class mounts its socket or named pipe: images, containers, and build cache persist
Processes, environment variables, and shell history State outside the node, such as databases, registries, and shared storage
Users, groups, and sudo rules created by an earlier job The kernel: all containers on a node share it
On Windows, the registry, the user profile, %TEMP%, and C:\ProgramData Data of finished containers that Swarm has not yet pruned from the node disk

The runner is mounted read-only, so a job cannot change what the next job runs (The runner distributor on Linux, The runner distributor on Windows). A single-task class needs no working directory cleanup, because the container is discarded. On Linux the runner does not clean it, because the runner user cannot remove files that the job user owns: the stack sets CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR to "false" (Working directory cleanup).

Containers are not a virtual machine boundary. Read Security before you run untrusted code.

The runner distributor on Linux

The Linux services use stock images such as cimg/base, and the image holds none of the runner. The service runner-distributor puts the runner on every Linux node that runs the classes of runners.yaml. docker stack deploy is the whole install, and the only upgrade path.

  • The service. runner-distributor is a global service from the stock alpine:3 image (pinned by digest), so it runs on every Linux node, also a Docker-build node and a node that joins later. A microVM node (machine-runner-swarm.microvm=true) is the exception: the microVM classes download their own runner into each VM (MicroVM jobs). Its script, linux/stack/runner-distributor.sh, is a Swarm config.
  • The volume. It writes to runner-bin, one named volume on every node. Each version has a directory versions/<version> with bin/circleci-runner, SHA256, VERSION, and TARBALL. The link current points to the active version and moves with one atomic rename. The file history lists the versions in the order they were active.
  • The runner services. Every class mounts runner-bin read-only at /opt/machine-runner-swarm. The entrypoint is another Swarm config, mounted at /circleci-runner-entrypoint with the mode 0555. A job cannot change either.
  • The wait. The entrypoint waits up to MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_WAIT seconds (default 120) until current exists, so a first deploy and a new node need no order. Without a runner, or with a binary that differs from its record, it exits with code 80, and Swarm retries after the restart delay.

A container resolves current once, so a running job keeps its version and the next container gets the new one. A persistent class runs one container for all jobs, so it picks up a new version when its container restarts (Recycle a class). The runner services carry no version and no hash: the version is a setting of the distributor service only, so an upgrade, a pin, and a rollback change that one service, and the runner services never restart. An idle replica keeps the old binary until it recycles, within the idle timeout of 1 hour.

MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_RUNNER_VERSION Behavior
3.1.13 (an exact version, the default: the newest that CI tests) A pin. The tarball is checked against the SHA-256 values that the stack file carries for it, not the manifest. It never changes by itself, makes no request once installed, and switches to an installed version without network, so a rollback needs no download. A release of this repository bumps the version and its SHA-256 values together
3.1 or 3 A floating line: the newest 3.1.x, or the newest 3.x.y, of CircleCI’s manifest. Checked again every 24 hours. It ignores the default SHA-256 list and trusts the hash of the manifest, which is weaker
current CircleCI’s current release, within major version 3. Checked again every 24 hours, and trusts the manifest hash like the floating lines

See The version policy for the rules, how this compares with machine runner 3, container runner and the orchestrator, Upgrade the runner on Linux for the settings, and Runner binary integrity on Linux for the checks.

The runner distributor on Windows

The Windows services use the stock Server Core image, with none of the runner and none of Git. The service runner-distributor-windows does what the Linux distributor does, with the same settings and version policy.

  • The service. A global service on the nodes with the label machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022, from the stock servercore:ltsc2022 image with process isolation. Its script, windows\stack\runner-distributor.ps1, is a Swarm config.
  • The volume and the links. It writes to runner-bin: versions\<version> for the runner (with SHA256, TARBALL and VERSION), git\<git version> for portable Git, and two relative directory symbolic links, current and git\current. Every class mounts the volume read-only twice, with volume.subpath: current at C:\machine-runner-swarm, and git\current at C:\Program Files\Git, where the task agent expects tar.exe.
  • No entrypoint. circleci-runner.exe is the main process. A runner task that starts before the first flip fails and starts again after the restart delay, so a new node needs no order. Nothing checks the binary when a container starts: Runner binary integrity on Windows.
  • Locked files. Windows cannot replace or delete files that a running container uses. The distributor installs a version next to the others, flips the link, and removes an old version only when no container uses it. No busy job is killed by an upgrade.

See Upgrade the runner on Windows for the settings.

Users and the runner token on Linux

Inside each Linux container, two accounts exist:

  • The runner user circleci-runner (uid 2000) runs circleci-runner and owns the token file. It has no sudo rights and cannot write to /opt/machine-runner-swarm.
  • The job user runs every job step. It is circleci in the cimg images, or the account you name with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_USER.

The runner steps each job down to the job user with command_prefix: sudo -niHu <job user> -- in the default class, setpriv when the image has no sudo, and always setpriv --no-new-privs in the hardened class. The token is never in the job environment, and the config file that the runner reads is readable only by the runner user and root. In the single-task classes that file holds the placeholder.

MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO decides the rest:

Class type Setting Jobs have sudo Can a job read the class token
Default (linux-default, and linux-java of classes-extra.yaml) "true" Yes, passwordless, as in the Docker executor No, the container holds a placeholder. Only a job that escapes onto the node of the proxy can
Hardened (linux-hardened of classes-extra.yaml) "false" No No, for the same reason
Persistent (linux-persistent, no proxy) "false" (the shipped file; "true" is the opt-in) No (with "true": yes) No, as in the hardened class. With "true", yes if the job uses sudo (The persistent class)

The default class. Jobs keep the passwordless sudo that many orgs and orbs expect, for example sudo apt-get install. A job that uses sudo is root in its container: it can read the placeholder and the files of the runner, and become the runner user, but it finds no class token (linux/tests/proxy.sh scans the containers as root to show it).

The hardened class. The entrypoint steps every job down with util-linux setpriv --no-new-privs, even when the image has sudo, and edits no file of the image. Swarm ignores no-new-privileges, so setuid binaries such as sudo and su stay in the image. The kernel flag that setpriv sets is inherited by the job and everything it starts, and cannot be cleared, so no setuid binary can lift a job to root, even through a local-root bug.

  • The container exits with code 80 if the image has no util-linux setpriv.
  • Jobs cannot install system packages at run time, and nothing in a job gains privileges through setuid or file capabilities (for example ping or mount). Build the tools into the image. CircleCI also recommends pre-installing dependencies as the most secure option.
  • A kernel or container-runtime bug can still lift a job to root, because the containers share the host kernel.

Choose the hardened class for shared or regulated work, and the default class for a single trusted team that needs sudo. See Security.

What the Linux entrypoint does

circleci-runner-entrypoint starts as root, prepares the container, and runs the runner as the runner user. It never reads the token or the placeholder. In order, it:

  1. Waits for the runner distributor, resolves current once, and checks the binary against its SHA-256 record. It also checks that the runner and every directory above it, up to /opt/machine-runner-swarm, are owned by root and not writable by the group or others.
  2. Looks for the tools it needs: sudo or util-linux setpriv to step jobs down, and setpriv or su to start the runner. With MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO=false, util-linux setpriv with --no-new-privs is required. Without the tools it exits with code 80 (What an image needs).
  3. Creates the users with useradd or adduser (sudo refuses a user that has no passwd and no shadow entry): circleci-runner with uid and gid 2000, and the job user when the image has none.
  4. Sets CIRCLECI_RUNNER_COMMAND_PREFIX. A value in the service environment does not override it.
    • With sudo, the prefix is ["sudo","-niHu","<job user>","--"]. The file /etc/sudoers.d/90-circleci-runner lets uid 2000 run commands as the job user only, and keeps the PATH and environment variables of the image.
    • Without sudo, or with MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO=false, it is a setpriv command that gives the job no capabilities (in the hardened class also --no-new-privs), run through env -u for every CIRCLECI_RUNNER_* and MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_* variable of the container (the runner name stays). The runner holds CAP_SETUID and CAP_SETGID as ambient capabilities only to call it.
  5. Creates the task agent and working directories, adds the job user to the group of /var/run/docker.sock when the class mounts the socket (Docker Builds), and runs the runner with exec as uid 2000. The init process (init: true) passes SIGTERM to it, which starts the runner drain.

It does not validate the runner name, the token, the mode, or the timeouts: the runner checks its own settings and exits with code 80 for a bad one. With sudo, a job gets the environment variables of the image (PATH, JAVA_HOME, LANG), the variables you set in the service (such as a proxy), and CIRCLECI_RUNNER_NAME, and nothing else from the runner.

Users and the runner token on Windows

Windows containers have no step-down: the runner and the jobs run as ContainerAdministrator, because the runner needs its symbolic link privilege to install the task agent. A job can read the config file of its runner. In a single-task class it holds only the placeholder (the class token is in token-proxy-windows), in the persistent class the real token. The token is not in the job environment. A hostile job on the same host as the proxy can still reach it, because process isolation is not a security boundary (Windows).

Treat each Windows resource class as a trust boundary: one token for each class, restricted users, rotated tokens. MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_SUDO and MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_JOB_USER do not exist on Windows. See Token model on each OS.

Placement

Services carry constraints and nodes advertise capabilities. The built-in properties are node.platform.os and node.platform.arch. This repository adds the node labels machine-runner-swarm.zone, machine-runner-swarm.docker-build, machine-runner-swarm.microvm, machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2022, machine-runner-swarm.windows-ltsc2025, and machine-runner-swarm.class.<service>. See Multi-Node Clusters.

Why Swarm and not plain Compose

A plain docker compose up restarts the same container, so the environment is not clean. Swarm creates a new container for every task. The FAQ lists the trade-offs.

Glossary

Term Meaning
Stack file A Compose-format YAML file that docker stack deploy reads: a main file (runners.yaml) for each OS and optional add-on stack files. This documentation never calls an add-on stack file an overlay, because an overlay network is a different thing
Stack The services that one docker stack deploy creates, named runners here, so the service linux-default is runners_linux-default in Swarm commands
Resource class, service A resource class is the CircleCI name, <namespace>/<name>, that a job selects with resource_class. A service is the Swarm object that runs it, named like the class without the namespace
runner-bin, current, record runner-bin is the named volume, one on every node, that holds the runner versions under versions/<version>. current is the link to the active version, which a container resolves once at start. The record is versions/<version>/SHA256, the SHA-256 of the binary in sha256sum -c format, which the entrypoint checks at every container start
Runner distributor The global service runner-distributor (Linux) or runner-distributor-windows (it installs portable Git too) that downloads, verifies, and installs the runner into runner-bin, moves current, and looks again every MACHINE_RUNNER_SWARM_CHECK_INTERVAL
Drain A runner drain happens when the runner gets SIGTERM: it takes no new job and finishes the running one. A node drain is docker node update --availability drain: Swarm stops the tasks of that node, which starts a runner drain in each, and starts replacements on other nodes. This documentation always says which one

item.title: Contributing
item.description:
Thank you for helping to improve the machine runner swarm. This repository is part of CircleCI Labs. Field engineering reviews issues and pull requests on a best-effort basis, with no SLA. CircleCI support does not cover this repository.

Reporting a bug

Search the existing issues first, and check that you use the latest release. Then open a new issue with the bug template. Include:

  • The release or commit of this repository, and the runner version. On Linux, run docker run --rm -v runners_runner-bin:/v:ro alpine cat /v/current/VERSION on the node. On Windows, run docker service logs --tail 100 runners_runner-distributor-windows.
  • The operating system of the node and the Docker Engine version.
  • The output of docker service ps --no-trunc runners_<service> and docker service logs --tail 100 runners_<service>.

Remove tokens, runner config files, and internal host names from everything you paste.

Security disclosure

Do not open a public issue for a security vulnerability. Email security@circleci.com and follow SECURITY.md.

Requesting a feature

Open an issue with the feature request template. Describe the problem, and name the platform and the files it affects. For problems in the CircleCI platform or the runner agent, contact CircleCI support instead.

Opening a pull request

Before you open a pull request:

  1. Discuss large changes in an issue first.
  2. Run the tests for the platform you changed (Development).
  3. Update docs/ when you change a variable, label, secret, port, or default.
  4. Write every commit message, and the pull request title, as a Conventional Commit (Commit messages). The release notes are generated from them, so there is no changelog entry to add.
  5. Check that the diff has no tokens, host names, or customer or vendor names. The repository is public.

A pull request from a fork gets no CI. The project builds no forked pull request and passes no secret to one (Secrets and public logs). A maintainer reads the change and, to run CI, pushes its commits to a branch of this repository by hand. Never push or mirror an outside branch to main or to a branch named smr-swarm/*: those names get the e2e runner tokens and, on main, the publishing contexts, and a job takes its configuration from its own branch.

A pull request that changes only documentation (docs/, site/, Markdown files) runs the lint jobs and the docs site build, and skips the builds and the Swarm tests (Documentation-only changes).

Use the pull request template. Maintainers choose the merge method: a squash merge turns the pull request title into the commit message on main, and a merge commit or rebase keeps your commits (Merge method).

Commit messages

Use Conventional Commits: type(scope): summary. The release job reads these messages to choose the version and write the release notes. Keep each commit small and atomic.

Type Use for
feat A new capability, or a changed stack-file contract
fix A bug fix
docs Documentation only
test Tests only
ci The CircleCI pipeline
chore Maintenance with no user-visible change
refactor, perf Code changes that keep behavior, or improve speed

Common scopes are linux, windows, docs, readme, and ci.

A breaking change appears first in the release notes, and while the version is 0.x it raises the minor number. Mark it in one of two ways, and write what the user has to change:

  • Add ! after the type or scope: feat(linux)!: rename the persistent service.

  • Add a BREAKING CHANGE: footer:

    feat(linux): rename the persistent service

BREAKING CHANGE: the service is now linux-persistent. Rename it in your stack file.

Development

Requirements: Docker with privileged containers for the Linux suite, bash, and PowerShell 7 for the Windows unit tests.

linux/tests/run-all.sh
linux/tests/run-all.sh token drain
linux/tests/stack-config.sh
pwsh -File windows/tests/Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 -InstallModules

The commands run the whole Linux suite, a subset, the stack file contract (no daemon needed), and the Windows unit tests (PSScriptAnalyzer and Pester).

The Linux tests run a Swarm inside docker:dind containers, so your own Docker engine never enters Swarm mode. Each test prints RESULT lines and exits 0 when it passes. CI runs the Windows Swarm tests on Windows Server 2022 and 2025. CI/CD lists the pipeline and every lint command.

CI runs the Linux groups as four parallel jobs, each with its own list (linux-swarm in .circleci/continue.yml). Add a new test to all in run-all.sh and to one of those lists: lint-circleci fails when a group is in no list or in two (Linux jobs without a token).

Test What it checks
stack-config.sh docker stack config for every combination of stack files, and the Swarm config names
helper.sh setup.sh --swarm-init, --secret and --deploy on a fresh Docker-in-Docker daemon
ephemerality.sh A new container for every job and no residue, with docker run --restart always as the negative control
exit80.sh The restart delay, no hot loop, and the exit codes 80 and 1 of the real runner
token.sh What a job can read in the default class and in the hardened class
task.sh The real runner runs tasks as the job user, also with CIRCLECI_RUNNER_CLEANUP_WORK_DIR=true and as a persistent runner
proxy.sh The token proxy image in a Swarm, in front of the real runner
placement.sh Placement on a manager and a worker, and docker-build.yaml
distributor.sh The runner-distributor service: install, upgrade, rollback, pins, floating versions, pruning, a tampered binary, a wrong SHA-256, and CircleCI’s real manifest. Needs network access
persistent.sh Continuous mode and persistent.yaml
microvm.sh The microVM add-on with Kata Containers. Skipped without /dev/kvm. Downloads Kata (about 1 GB) unless SWARM_TEST_KATA_DIR or SWARM_TEST_KATA_TARBALL points at a copy. Not part of run-all.sh
drain.sh SIGTERM during a job: the job finishes
limits.sh init, ulimits, pids, memory, CPU, reservations, and the capability sets
network.sh Network isolation between classes, and between the replicas of a class
container-mode.sh The prototype container agent in a Swarm, against a fake API. Needs the Go and pause images
bats/run.sh The entrypoint unit tests on cimg/base, Alpine, and UBI minimal

The suite needs no installed runner: the distributor of the shipped stack installs one from a small HTTP mirror in the harness. Most tests publish fake-runner.sh, and task.sh, token.sh, exit80.sh, placement.sh, distributor.sh and the idle case of drain.sh publish the real runner binary, which the harness downloads once and checks against the SHA-256 of CircleCI’s manifest.

Three variables change the setup: SWARM_TEST_DIND_IMAGE sets the Docker-in-Docker image, SWARM_TEST_CACHE sets the directory that caches the real runner binary (~/.cache/swarm-tests by default), and SWARM_TEST_KEEP=1 keeps the containers for debugging.

The Windows tests in windows/tests print CHECK <name> PASS|FAIL lines and one RESULT line, and exit 0 only when every check passes. Invoke-UnitTests.ps1 runs the Pester tests on any system with PowerShell 7. The Test-*.ps1 scripts (Injection, Ephemerality, Exit80, Placement, StopHandling, Install, Distributor and Persistent) need a Windows host with Docker in Windows-container mode and no runner token.
